title: Infanteer (CAF)
employer: The Cameron Highlanders of Ottawa (Duke of Edinburgh's Own)
description: Infantry Soldiers are the Army's primary combat fighters and are responsible for closing with and engaging the enemy. They are the core members of the Combat Arms team, which includes Artillery and Armoured Soldiers. Infantry Soldiers are capable of operating anywhere in the world in any environment and in any combination of arms, including airmobile and amphibious operations. The primary duties of an Infantry Soldier are to: Expertly operate and maintain a wide range of weapons, including rifle, hand-grenades, light, medium and heavy machine-guns, and anti-tank weapons Use sophisticated equipment for field communications, navigation and night-vision surveillance Inspect and maintain weapon systems, vehicles, survival gear and personal defensive equipment Participate in airborne operations Operate with support elements such as fighter aircraft, tactical and artillery Engage in unarmed combat Employ camouflage and concealment, patrol, assault, defence, and escape-and-evasion tactics. Infantry Soldiers normally work outdoors. Both in training and on operations they live and work in conditions that would resemble those in the field. Infantry Soldiers will be posted to a battalion in Canada, but there are employment opportunities across Canada and on deployed operations around the world. To start a full or part-time career in the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) you must: Be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident Be at least 18 years old (17 years old with parental consent), except: For the Paid Education programs - you may be 16 years old (with parental consent) For the Primary Reserves-you may be 16 years old (with parental consent) and must be enrolled as a full-time student Have completed at least Grade 10 or 24 credits of Secondary IV in Quebec (some jobs need higher levels of education) If you have completed your education outside Canada, you must have your Educational Credential Assessments (ECAs) completed for your high school and highest level of education prior to submitting your application. For more information about eligibility requirements or the application process, please visit Joining the Forces . You can submit your application even if you are not sure about the job-specific requirements. Once we get your application, we'll work with you to determine if you qualify. If you have questions at any time throughout the process or you'd like to know which part-time jobs are available in your area, you can visit our Help Centre or Contact Us .

title: VDC Mechanical Coordinator
description: Job purpose The VDC Mechanical Coordinator, reporting to the VDC Manager, supports the preparation and coordination of mechanical design documents and BIM models, with a primary focus on HVAC systems and exposure to plumbing coordination. Working closely with Lar-Mex's project team, the VDC Mechanical Coordinator will assist in developing coordinated mechanical system models and drawings while receiving mentorship and hands-on training from experienced team members. This role offers valuable exposure to real-world project coordination and mechanical construction practices. Duties and responsibilities Job Duties: • Assist in interpreting plans and specifications to support the development of practical and efficient mechanical system designs. • Support the preparation of mechanical system drawings, BIM models, and coordination documents with guidance from the VDC team. • Assist in coordinating drawings and design information with Project Managers to ensure project requirements are met. • Participate in coordination meetings with internal project teams, consultants, and subcontractors. • Help identify and resolve design clashes and coordination issues within BIM models. • Work closely with project teams to support accurate and coordinated design documentation. • Assist in maintaining accurate models that align with project specifications and installation requirements. • Support the preparation of sleeving, layout, and pre-fabrication drawings for construction teams. • Participate in site visits to gain field exposure and assist with drawing verification. • Provide regular progress updates to the VDC Manager and seek guidance when required. • Support the VDC team in maintaining quality and consistency across project models. • Perform other duties as assigned to support project and team objectives. Qualifications Knowledge and Abilities: • Basic understanding of mechanical building systems, including HVAC; exposure to plumbing systems is considered an asset. • Familiarity with BIM software such as Revit and Navisworks through education, co-op placements, or project work. • General understanding of construction drawings and coordination processes. • Willingness to learn mechanical coordination practices and develop technical expertise through mentorship and hands-on experience. Required Skills: • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written. • Positive attitude and willingness to learn in a team-based environment. • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. • Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines. • Adaptability and willingness to take initiative when solving problems. • Ability to work collaboratively with project and field teams. Considered an Asset: • Co-op, internship, or project experience related to BIM, drafting, or mechanical systems. • Exposure to construction or mechanical contracting environments. • Understanding of mechanical assembly or installation methods. • Bilingual written and oral proficiency in English and French.

title: Early Childhood Educator (ECE) - Montessori Classroom Assistant & Elementary Support
description: Description Bhakta Prahlad Montessori School is seeking an Early Childhood Educator to join our teaching team. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys working with children across multiple age groups and appreciates the variety that comes with being part of a growing school. Working alongside experienced Montessori educators, the successful candidate will primarily support our Montessori Casa classrooms (ages 2.5 to 6 years), with opportunities to contribute to our lower elementary program and before and after school care, depending on qualifications, experience, and the needs of the school. Qualifications and experience in the Vaishnava Bhakti tradition (ISKCON) is an asset. The ideal candidate is charismatic, builds respectful relationships with children, has a natural ability to understand others' needs, is flexible and able to adapt to the needs of the program that come with working in a close-knit school community rather than that within a traditional school model. Responsibilities Responsibilities will vary based on qualifications and experience and may include: Support, create or implement a curriculum that promotes children's physical, cognitive, emotional, social, and practical life development. Lead or assist with the daily operation of a Montessori Casa classroom. Prepare and maintain a safe, organized, and engaging learning environment using Montessori principles and incorporating values of the Vaishnava Bhakti tradition. Observe children's interests, behaviour, and developmental progress, maintaining accurate records and documentation. Assess children's abilities and discuss observations and progress with families and colleagues. Support children's independence, concentration, confidence, and positive social interactions through respectful guidance. Guide children in developing practical life skills, self-care routines, conflict resolution, and self-regulation. Lead or participate in activities including storytelling, music, art, outdoor learning, movement Support lower elementary students with classroom routines and learning activities, where appropriate. Plan and organize activities for school-age children attending our before and after school program. Assist children with eating, dressing, toileting, diapering, handwashing, rest periods, and other daily care routines as needed. Prepare snacks and assist with meal routines. Maintain classroom materials, equipment, and learning resources. Ensure the health, safety, and well-being of all children while following licensing requirements and school policies. Communicate professionally with parents regarding children's daily experiences and developmental progress. Participate in staff meetings, collaborative planning, and ongoing professional development. About Our School Bhakta Prahlad Montessori School is an independent multi-age Montessori school located in Russell, Ontario. We currently operate three licensed Montessori Casa classrooms for children aged 2.5-6 years, offer before and after school care for neighbouring schools, and provide a multi-age elementary program. We have been operating for 10 years and continue to place an emphasis and value on genuine relationships. We believe in a holistic education model, nurturing mind, body and soul. The outstanding characters of the educators will be what shapes the character development of the children in their classrooms, and therefore we are looking for a unique individual to imbibe the teachings of bhakti and the qualities of a vaishnava. Educators have opportunities to contribute beyond a single classroom, share their individual strengths, and continue developing professionally as our programs evolve. Why Join Us? We're looking for someone who is seeking more than simply a job. We encourage initiative, offer regular professional development opportunities through our educational network, and provide the chance to take on increased responsibilities as our school continues to develop. If you're looking for a unique work environment, where relationships matter, and every day brings something a little different, we warmly invite your application. title: Student Procurement Officer (PART TIME)
description: Student Procurement Officer (PART TIME) Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC)/ Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC) Student Procurement Officer Finance and Awards Administration Division National Capital Region NSERC and SSHRC are looking for a part-time student (15 to 22.5 hours per week) to support our Procurement and Contracting team. We are seeking a motivated, action-oriented team player who is interested in supporting a dynamic procurement environment and eager to develop new skills. This is a great opportunity to gain hands-on experience while contributing to a collaborative and fast-paced team. Who we Are The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) funds visionaries, explorers and innovators who are searching for the scientific and technical breakthroughs that will benefit our country. We are Canada's largest supporter of discovery and innovation. We work with universities, colleges, businesses and not-for-profits to remove barriers, develop opportunities and attract new expertise to make Canada's research community thrive. We give Canadian scientists and engineers the means to go further because we believe in research without borders and beyond frontiers. The Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) is the federal research funding agency that promotes and supports research and research training in the humanities and social sciences. Through its Talent, Insight and Connection programs, and through partnerships and collaborations, SSHRC strategically supports world-leading initiatives that reflect a commitment to ensuring a better future for Canada and the world. SSHRC also oversees the delivery of a number of tri-agency programs, including the Canada Research Chairs and other research chairs programs, and the New Frontiers in Research Fund , which supports international, interdisciplinary, fast-breaking and high-risk research. Description of Duties Reporting to a Senior Procurement Advisor for the Procurement and Contracting group, the position provides contracting and procurement advice and services to Cost Centre (CC) Managers and Project Authorities (PAs) by planning and delivering the procurement of low dollar value requirements (below $25,000 for goods and below $40,000 for services) for low to medium complexity (risk) goods and services. This includes requirements such as call-ups against standing offers, low dollar value purchase orders; and requirements which fall under Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) and Shared Services Canada (SSC) for mandatory procurement instruments, including IT requirements. Responsibilities: Analyze client requirements, specification and requisition documents, review the adequacy of statements of work/ statements of requirements in order to plan and deliver procurement of low dollar value requirements (below $25,000 goods, $40,000 services) and low to medium complexity (risk) goods and services. Essential Qualifications Requirement: - must be returning to school in Winter term Official Language English essential Education Enrollment in a Supply Chain and Operations Management program (or equivalent) Experience Experience in a client service environment; Experience using Microsoft Office; Experience reviewing documentation; and Experience providing administrative support services Abilities Ability to plan/organize and address priorities Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing Ability to evaluate problems and suggest effective solutions Ability to analyze proposals and contractual documents Ability to work under pressure and with conflicting demands Ability to provide advice and guidance to clients Personal Suitabilities Strong interpersonal skills Client service orientation Results orientation Team-oriented Adaptable to ongoing change Autonomy, flexibility, accuracy, initiative and judgment Asset Qualifications Experience working in a procurement/financial system (such as SAP) Bilingual - Proficiency in both official languages Conditions of Employment • Adherence to the NSERC Code of Conduct; • Adherence to the NSERC Conflict of Interest and Post-Employment Policy; • Compliance with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector; • Legal status to accept employment for the entire period of employment; and • Reliability security clearance Work Location Hybrid between telework and Zibi Building (125 Zaida Eddy Private, 5th floor, Ottawa ON) Should you be interested in this opportunity, please apply and submit your resume and cover letter through the Algonquin College HireAC portal. title: Respiratory Therapist, Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) - BC Women's Hospital & Health Centre
description: Respiratory Therapist, Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) BC Women's Hospital & Health Centre Vancouver, BC Advance Your Career in Neonatal Intensive Care at BC Women's Hospital + Health Centre **Relocation expenses up to $5,000 available for qualified candidates! Are you passionate about making a profound difference in the lives of newborns and their families? Join the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) at BC Women's Hospital + Health Centre - a world leader in specialized neonatal care and the sole provincial quaternary referral centre serving British Columbia and the Yukon. Here, you'll develop a specialized expertise in neonatal care and transport, caring for both fragile newborns and their mothers. Our unique family-centered design features 70 single-family rooms that keep mothers, newborns, and families together-because healing happens best when families are united. As a key member of our multidisciplinary team, you'll collaborate closely with nurses and physicians to deliver exceptional care. You'll be part of a dedicated resuscitation team for high-risk deliveries and urgent neonatal care scenarios, making life-saving impacts every day. Our NICU Respiratory Therapists also lead the way in neonatal transport, working alongside BC Emergency Health Services and BC Ambulance Services to provide critical respiratory support during transfers - a unique and highly valued role. At BCW NICU, education is embedded into your daily schedule, with integrated multidisciplinary learning opportunities designed to advance your skills and professional growth. You'll also have the rewarding opportunity to teach families how to care for their newborns confidently at home, making a difference that extends beyond the hospital walls. If you're ready to join a cutting-edge, supportive environment where innovation, compassion, and family-centered care come first, the NICU at BC Women's Hospital is the perfect place to grow your career. Watch this video to better envision your dream career in the NICU at BC Women's Hospital What you'll do Review patient's medical history, conduct assessments of the patient's pathophysical condition, recommend appropriate care and document patient response and outcomes. Set up, checks, perform specified quality control procedures and operate respiratory equipment, making adjustments as appropriate. Initiate, monitor and assess ventilator dependent patients as per care protocols and daily care. Recommend and administer individualized medical gas therapies. Provide invasive and non-invasive cardio-pulmonary monitoring. Evaluate patient's responses during testing, therapies and related treatments; make changes as appropriate; observe and record data on patient chart. Respond to cardiac arrests and other emergency calls. Prepare reports, statistical information and summaries of research activities as required. Attend departmental and program meetings to provide or exchange information. Participate in departmental, program and health centre committees. Participate in the education and mentoring of students, staff members, physicians and other health care professionals. Perform other related duties as assigned. Current and continuing registration with British Society of Respiratory Therapists (BCSRT) and the Canadian Society of Respiratory Therapists (CSRT). Current Basic Life Support certification. title: MRO Shop Supervisor - Aircraft Component
description: Position Overview MHD-ROCKLAND is a global leader in fixed-wing aircraft parts, services, and aftermarket support, with more than 40 years of experience supporting military and commercial legacy fleets worldwide. Through our strategic global locations and qualified repair network, we provide inventory management, spares, rotables, in-house MRO (maintenance, repair, and overhaul capabilities) as well as manage a large network of outside service providers that ensure aircraft are mission ready. MHDR operates globally and has offices in Canada, USA, Australia, and New Zealand. We are currently seeking an experienced MRO Shop Supervisor - Aircraft Component for our Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, QC location. In this hands-on role, you will lead aircraft component shop operations, supervise repair technicians, and help ensure work is completed safely, efficiently, and in line with customer and regulatory requirements. You will remain involved in day-to-day shop floor activities while coordinating with internal teams to support production priorities, material availability, quality, and on-time delivery. Main Duties and Responsibilities Lead a team of dedicated technicians and support staff to achieve planned outcomes; Oversee daily production progress, adjust priorities as needed, and ensure the right personnel, equipment, tools, technical data, spares, and supplies are in place to meet turnaround times, production schedules, and delivery commitments; Coordinate with Supply Chain to address material shortages, urgent requirements, production changes, parts availability, consumables, and external repairs while ensuring compliance, alignment with priorities, and support for on-time operations; Collect key indices and present them to the management team; Ensure all personnel authorized to perform or supervise maintenance are adequately trained on applicable regulations and company procedures; Ensure that all personnel observe the AMO's policies and codes of conduct; Ensure maintenance records, inspection documents, and shop paperwork are accurate, complete, and properly maintained; Support quality investigations, corrective actions, audit findings, and continuous improvement initiatives. Monitor shop KPIs such as turnaround time, productivity, rework, on-time delivery, quality and safety performance; Perform work in accordance with the Maintenance Policy Manual (MPM) and Transport Canada regulatory standards and serve as back up to the Person Responsible for Maintenance (PRM) as designated for TCCA; Ensure that all personnel observe workplace health and safety requirements and wear the appropriate personal safety equipment while at work; Perform other duties and assignments as directed by management. Requirements and Core Competencies Transport Canada AME certification; Aircraft or component maintenance experience; Knowledge of TCCA Civil Aviation Regulations; Experience managing a team of technicians; Excellent English communication skills (written and spoken). Bilingualism is an asset; Detail-oriented & highly organized with the ability to adapt to shifting priorities in a production environment; Ability to work shifts, if required, to support business needs; Ability to travel (occasional); Comfortable using Microsoft 365; Comfortable using ERP systems.

title: Personal Support Worker
description: The Personal Support Worker provides direct support to individuals with developmental disabilities, dual diagnoses, autism spectrum disorder, acquired brain injuries, or mental health challenges who require specialized behavioural supports. The Support Worker promotes independence, dignity, safety, and quality of life by implementing Behaviour Support Plans (BSPs), teaching positive coping strategies, and supporting individuals in achieving their personal goals. Key Responsibilities Behavioural Support Implement individualized Behaviour Support Plans (BSPs) as developed by the clinical team. Utilize evidence-based positive behaviour support strategies. Monitor, document, and report behavioural observations, incidents, and progress. Recognize triggers and early warning signs and implement proactive intervention strategies. Use approved de-escalation techniques while maintaining the safety of residents and staff. Participate in behavioural data collection and tracking. Support crisis interventions in accordance with organizational policies. Direct Resident Support Assist individuals with activities of daily living (ADLs) including personal hygiene, dressing, toileting, and meal preparation as required. Promote independence and skill development. Support community participation, recreation, employment, and volunteer activities. Foster meaningful relationships while maintaining professional boundaries. Encourage choice, inclusion, and person-centred planning. Health & Safety Administer medications as delegated and trained. Follow all medication administration policies and documentation requirements. Respond appropriately to medical emergencies and behavioural crises. Follow infection prevention and control procedures. Complete incident reports and serious occurrence documentation when required. Ensure a safe and clean living environment. Documentation Complete shift notes and communication logs accurately. Record behavioural data and complete ABC charts as required. Document interventions and outcomes objectively. Communicate significant changes to supervisors and the interdisciplinary team. Team Collaboration Participate in team meetings, case conferences, and training. Collaborate with Behaviour Therapists, Social Workers, families, healthcare professionals, and community partners. Provide mentorship and guidance to new staff regarding Behaviour Support Plans. Maintain confidentiality in accordance with organizational policies and legislation. Knowledge & Skills Strong understanding of Positive Behaviour Support principles. Experience implementing Behaviour Support Plans. Knowledge of Applied Behaviour Analysis (ABA) principles is considered an asset. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Strong conflict resolution and crisis intervention abilities. Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Excellent organizational and time management skills. Ability to maintain professionalism in high-stress situations. Physical Requirements Ability to safely assist with transfers and mobility. Ability to stand, walk, bend, lift, and provide physical support throughout the shift. Ability to respond quickly during behavioural or medical emergencies. Working Conditions Days, evenings, weekends, holidays, and overnight shifts as required. Work in residential homes and community settings. Exposure to challenging behaviours, medical needs, and crisis situations. May be required to work independently or as part of a team. Core Competencies Person-Centred Support Positive Behaviour Support Professionalism Compassion and Empathy Crisis Prevention and Intervention Teamwork Communication Accountability Problem Solving Adaptability Respect and Inclusion Expectations Employees are expected to: Treat all individuals with dignity, respect, and compassion. Follow all organizational policies, Behaviour Support Plans, and health and safety procedures. Maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries. Attend mandatory training and maintain required certifications. Contribute to a positive, respectful, and collaborative workplace culture. Hours of Work: Thurs 2pm-9pm Fri 2pm-9pm Saturday 7am-2pm Some Sundays to meet staffing requirements. This job description is intended to outline the general duties and responsibilities of the Personal Support Worker position and may be amended as operational requirements evolve. Qualifications Required Minimum one year experience supporting individuals with complex behavioural needs (preferred). Valid Standard First Aid and CPR-C. Current Criminal Record Check with Vulnerable Sector Screening. Valid Class G Driver's Licence with a clean driver's abstract. Reliable transportation.

description: Join a chef-led artisan bakery focused on craftmanship, fermentation, and great taste. title: Cardiology Technologist
description: We are seeking a Permanent Part Time Cardiology Technologist at Vernon Jubilee Hospital in Vernon, BC. Days of work: Rotating, Days Shift times: 08:00 to 16:30 What we offer: • Employee & Family Assistance Program • Employer paid training/education opportunities • Employer paid vacation • Extended health & dental coverage • May be eligible for Municipal Pension Plan • Work-life balance A Relocation Allowance package may be offered with the position. Applicable positions may qualify for up to $15,000 as a recruitment incentive. What will you work on? The Cardiology Technologist performs techniques relating to Electro Cardiogram (ECG) testing, stress testing, Holter and event Recorders and pacemaker monitoring and other types of diagnostic cardiac equipment. • Explains procedures to prepare patients for testing such as ECG, stress testing, Holter monitoring, pacemaker monitoring, ambulatory blood pressure monitoring and related tests and answers related questions. • Performs a variety of non-invasive examinations such as ECG, stress testing and Holter and event monitoring and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring by attaching electrodes to the patient, operating equipment, analyzing and recording relevant data for interpretation by cardiologist and/or internist. • Explains cardiac pacemaker screen system to patients, monitors cardiac pacemakers and notifies cardiologist and/or internist of abnormalities; contacts patients by telephone for repeat recordings as required. • Monitors patients and scans test strips during cardiograms and stress tests and takes appropriate action upon recognition of cardiac arrhythmias or other abnormalities in accordance with established policies and procedures. • Scans and analyzes ECG, stress, Holter and event monitor, and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring test strips. Selects and assesses appropriate portions of test strips and summarizes for interpretation by medical staff in accordance with established policies and procedures. • Transfers and assigns ECGs in ECG Cardiology Management systems (i.e. Tracemaster) for interpretation by medical staff. • Demonstrates ECG testing procedures and operation of related equipment as required. • Monitors ongoing departmental activity levels and assists fellow staff to meet requests for service. • Maintains statistics and files completed reports. • Maintains equipment by cleaning, lubricating and replacing items such as paper rolls, electrodes, and leads. • Participates in Quality Management and/or Quality Assurance programs (including LEAN projects/initiatives) by providing information and input to Manager (or designate) • Participates in the instruction/orientation of staff and/or students by assisting with departmental orientations, in-service presentations, demonstrating procedures and answering questions, as required. • Maintains and updates own clinical knowledge within area of practice. • Performs other related duties as assigned. description: ADMINISTRATIVE ASSOCIATE, NATIONAL CREATION FUND AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT Competition number: J0826-0306 Department: National Creation Fund and Professional Development Status: Full-Time Term (end date: August 31, 2028) Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (35 hours per week) Annual/hourly salary: $65,000 - $81,200 (position with benefits and pension plan) Closing date: September 20th, 2026 Anticipated start date: as soon as possible Introducing the National Arts Centre The National Arts Centre (NAC) is Canada's bilingual, multi-disciplinary home for the performing arts. The NAC presents, creates, produces, and co-produces performing arts programming in various streams - the NAC Orchestra, Dance, English Theatre, French Theatre, Indigenous Theatre, and Popular Music and Variety - and nurtures the next generation of audiences and artists from across Canada. The NAC is located in the National Capital Region on the unceded territory of the Anishinabe Algonquin Nation. At the National Arts Centre, we believe the performing arts are vital to the human experience. A house of dreams for the Canadian performing arts, we work with artists and arts organizations from across this land to revitalize our sector. Curious to learn more? Read our 2023-2026 Strategic Plan, The Journey Ahead . Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, Anti-Racism and Accessibility We are on a journey, committed to ensuring that equity, diversity, inclusion, accessibility, anti-racism and reconciliation with Indigenous peoples will guide our actions. The NAC welcomes applications from?candidates who can help us meet our vision, and contribute to the diversity of?lived experiences, perspectives, and approaches.?When you join the NAC, you will be part of an inclusive?community working hard to dismantle barriers to employees'?well-being, access, potential, and success. The NAC actively seeks candidates who identify as women, Indigenous, Black, Persons of Colour (IBPoC), members of 2SLGBTQIA+ communities, and people?with disabilities. We encourage you to self-identify in the recruitment process. About the National Creation Fund and Professional Development The National Arts Centre's National Creation Fund is dedicated to the alchemy of artistic creation and driven by a conviction in the power of creation as a means of evolving culture, sparking innovation, and shaping our world. The Fund champions creation through transformative investments in the development of bold new music, dance, theatre and interdisciplinary performances, and through our work as a home for research and experimentation on the conditions required to create ambitious work. The NAC Professional Development team produces high-impact programs for artists and arts professionals, including apprenticeships, mentorships, and intensives. Key activities: Under the direction of the Artistic Producer, National Creation Fund, the Administrative Associate is the administrative backbone of the National Creation Fund and Professional Development teams, providing administrative, operational, and logistical support to both teams. This role provides high-level administrative and operational support across both departments, playing a pivotal role in the National Creation Fund's submission and investment processes and the planning and execution of Professional Development's suite of residencies, gatherings, and apprenticeships. Working closely with members of the Creation Fund and Professional Development teams, the Administrative Associate helps ensure both departments run smoothly and effectively, offering our communities and partners a meaningful experience. The incumbent is a key administrative resource, supporting multiple areas while maintaining strong attention to detail, positive relationships, and organizational effectiveness. Working closely with department leadership and team members, the Administrative Associate serves as a trusted partner in planning, problem-solving, and implementing priorities while ensuring operational excellence. Department Operations and Administration Respond to inquiries from artists, participants, partners, and arts organizations; Maintain the flow of the Fund's submission process by coordinating with our curatorial teams, booking meetings, circulating prep material, identifying and securing access support and interpretation, to ensure curatorial decisions are made and shared in a timely manner; Establish and maintain digital document management systems, electronic filing systems, databases, templates, and administrative records; Track, organize, and maintain department files, applications, submissions, agreements, reports, and supporting documentation; Assist with the administration and drafting of agreements and reporting; Prepare correspondence, meeting materials, agendas, presentations, reports, and briefing documents; Coordinate translation requests and assist with the preparation of bilingual materials; Identify and book access support measures as needed; Support the management of the Fund's National Advisory Committee, including booking meetings, organizing and executing meeting logistics, preparing and circulating advance materials, and onboarding new members; Schedule departmental meetings, maintain weekly meeting records and departmental Outlook Calendar; Recommend and implement administrative improvements that may enhance efficiency, organization, or experience; Support departmental financial administration, including expense claims, procurement forms, purchase requests, credit card reports, recurring payments, and payment documentation; Manage invoices and process payments, and ensure timely payments due under various contracts; Act as principal departmental liaison with NAC Finance Department for administration matters; Maintain and update the contact list and manage invite and RSVP lists for performances, as well as ticket allocation and distribution. Company Management and Event Support Coordinate travel arrangements, accommodations, per diems, transportation, and logistics for the department. Prepare and process travel approvals and travel claims; Execute logistics for ancillary events, team retreats, premieres etc., as well as residencies, leadership programs, advisory meetings, workshops, receptions, and special initiatives. Logistics include room bookings, catering requests, performance tickets, and accessibility measures; Provide on-site administrative and logistical support before, during and after programs and events, including responding to evolving needs, coordinating schedule changes, and assisting staff. External Relationship Management Administrative contact for participants, artists, curators, National Advisory Committee members, external partners, and service providers; Maintain relationships with partners by coordinating information requests, meetings, materials, and logistics; Support participant communications before, during, and after programs and event; Communications Support Assist with updating websites, gathering materials for social media and securing approvals for communications materials; Execute the collection, organization and approvals of quotes, photos, and videos for communications purposes. Required qualifications: Post-secondary degree, in a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience; Minimum of three (3) years of related experience in administrative roles with significant responsibilities; Demonstrated attention to detail and accuracy, with a strong degree of professionalism, tact, and diplomacy; Exceptional interpersonal and communications skills; Fluently bilingual in both official languages, French and English, written and spoken; Strong organizational and administrative skills; Proven ability to develop, streamline and continuously optimize operational processes; Highly organized and able to coordinate a variety of activities simultaneously; Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (including Microsoft Teams, Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint), and Adobe; Ability to adapt quickly in a rapidly evolving environment; Strong digital literacy and ability to learn new technologies and systems; Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and take ownership of tasks; Collaborative team player, adept at working within a complex organizational structure; Experience contributing to the administrative support of a busy department within a large organization; A demonstrated interest and/or work experience in the performing arts or cultural sector is an asset; Experience creating visually engaging materials, presentations or communications, with an eye for design, creativity, and user experience is preferred; Weekend and evening work performing event-related tasks is occasionally required.

title: Firearms Officer B/L
description: The Ministry of the Solicitor General, Ontario Provincial Police, and the Chief Firearms Office are seeking a qualified individual to join our Licensing Unit. In this exciting, rewarding and challenging opportunity, you will be responsible for processing firearms license applications and to providing firearms licensing support and related services to the public and to Municipal, Provincial and Federal Agencies. Please note: The successful candidate will be expected to work out of the Ottawa or Sudbury work location, five (5) days a week. About Us: The Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) is one of North America's largest deployed police services with more than 6,400 uniformed officers, 2,900 civilian employees and 530 Auxiliary officers. We provide essential services that ensure the safety and security of the people of the Province of Ontario. The OPP is a division of the Ministry of the Solicitor General, the largest operational ministry in the province with a presence in every community across Ontario. We are the largest police service in Ontario and the second largest in Canada. The mandate of the Chief Firearms Office (CFO) is to protect public safety through the administration of the licensing provisions of the Firearms Act and Regulations. The Chief Firearms Officer for the Province of Ontario is delegated authority under the Act by the Minister of the Solicitor General, and is responsible for the administration and delivery of these key components of the Firearms Act. The OPP Values promote always doing the right things for the right reasons, by: Serving with PRIDE, PROFESSIONALISM and HONOUR. Interacting with RESPECT, COMPASSION and FAIRNESS. Leading with INTEGRITY, HONESTY and COURAGE. About the job Do you have the ability to deliver high?volume operational and administrative support in a dynamic environment, managing confidential information across multiple systems, responding to inquiries, and promoting firearms licensing through public outreach and education? In this exciting position you will process and assess firearms licence applications, transfers, and authorizations, by conducting detailed screenings, database reviews, and eligibility decisions to protect public safety. Additionally, you will act as a critical point of contact for the public, law enforcement, and justice partners, conducting interviews, responding to safety concerns, providing expert guidance on the Firearms Act, and supporting investigations and court processes. What you bring to the team Mandatory: Ability to pass an OPP background/ security investigation. Oral and written French Language skills at the advanced level Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Working knowledge of federal and provincial FOI requirements to ensure appropriate information sharing, along with strong understanding of the firearms licensing program to clearly explain eligibility and accurately direct inquiries. Proficiency with office and operational systems (e.g., Word, Excel, Outlook, CFIS, RMS, CPIC, Cognos) to accurately process applications, manage data entry, track application status, generate reports, and maintain organized records, along with effective use of standard office equipment. We strive to maintain a resident's physical abilities which creates a sense of personal well being, and independence. We support our resident's spiritual care needs and continued connection with their community through our volunteer networks. We are a regulated health care service provider governed by the Fixing Long-Term Care Act (2021) and its supporting Regulations. Lanark Lodge is accredited through CARF Canada. CARF accreditation is an external peer-review that recognized Lanark Lodge for meeting high standards in quality, safety, and continuous improvement. Key Duties and Responsibilities 1. Answer call signals and respond to residents' needs promptly and respectfully. 4. Weigh, lift, turn, and position residents safely. 5. Make beds and maintain residents' rooms. 6. Transport residents by wheelchair or stretcher as required. 7. Serve meal trays and assist with feeding where needed. 8. Supply and empty bed pans and assist with personal care duties. 9. Collect specimens where required. 10. Administer first aid in emergency situations. 11. Perform light housekeeping and cleaning duties related to resident care. 12. Provide companionship and support to residents. 13. Perform other duties related to patient care, comfort, and personal care, consistent with the position. Work Conditions and Physical Demands Fast-paced environment, physically demanding work, repetitive tasks, standing for extended periods, bending, crouching, kneeling, walking, and a combination of sitting, standing, and walking. title: Advisor, Community Outreach and Programs
description: A Brief Overview The Yellow House Student Centre for Equity & Inclusion team is committed to creating comfortable and accountable spaces for students who identify as Queer, Trans, Black, Indigenous, and/or as People of Colour (QTBIPoC) to feel safe, to create community, to be empowered, to celebrate their identity and to flourish. We seek to engage students in initiatives that actively dismantle oppressive, racist and colonial ideologies and practices. title: Supervisor, Operations
description: Reporting to the Manager, Shift Operations, Custodial Support Services (Manager), the Supervisor, Operations (Supervisor) is a member of the Custodial Support Services (CSS) leadership team. The Supervisor works closely and collaboratively with the Manager to direct custodial activities in order to implement the published Service Level Standards (SLS) as it pertains to the respective shift. The client-centric Supervisor engages with frontline custodial staff through formal and informal discussions relating to scope of work execution and performance. Accountable to validate the SLS by completing quality assurance (QA) audits, the Supervisor is responsible for engaging with frontline custodial staff to remove roadblocks preventing them from executing their work. The Supervisor works collaboratively with the Manager, to initiate the performance improvement process to correct behaviour and address audit issues as required. The Supervisor also participates in the recruitment process and in collaboration with the Manager, is responsible for the hands-on orientation of new staff ensuring that custodial staff are trained and comply with all university, Facilities, and CSS' health and safety policies and procedures and ensures staff competency in the safe use and maintenance of equipment. The Supervisor is expected to be knowledgeable of a variety of cleaning products, chemicals, tools and equipment, to stay current with industry trends, and to make suggestions for increasing the effectiveness and efficiency of custodial support services. The Supervisor works an assigned shift; however, must also be available to work flexible hours as required, including weekends. In addition, the Supervisor is on a rotating call-in list for emergency calls from the Emergency Response Centre. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: • Plan, execute and manage frequency based quality control audits each shift to ensure SLS targets are achieved, with the intention of getting through all spaces on campus on a determined frequency. • Collaborate with the Managers to provide consistent, decisive leadership for all custodial staff. • Manage, train, coach, and mentor custodial staff to ensure assigned facilities are cleaned in compliance with the SLS. • Connect with custodial staff in the field on a routine basis to, among other reasons, engage in conversations regarding work requirements, health and safety related issues impacting their scope of work, performance management, and to reinforce the importance of the work performed. • Escalate issues of poor performance or poor audit outcomes, building users concerns, staffing challenges and training requirements to the Manager for support as needed, if no support is required, provide a debrief to the Manager. • Working with the Manager, train and monitor custodial staff on the safe and proper operation of all cleaning products and equipment ensuring that items requiring repair or maintenance, are addressed in a timely manner. • Ensure that custodial staff properly clean equipment each shift and that equipment, supplies and tools are properly replaced, re-stocked, and secured at the end of the shift. • Complete requests for supplies and equipment, in order to have adequate inventory levels in compliance with the CSS Procurement Policy. • Communicate and work collaboratively with the Manager to ensure alignment relating to operational conditions that arise. • Ensure that university supplied workwear and staff identification is prominently worn by all custodial staff while on shift; ensure that all custodial staff wear safety footwear. • Working in alignment with the Manager, manage the client service relationships within assigned facilities as required. • Assist in the development, coordination and delivery of training programs. • Participate in mandatory engagement town hall meetings and ensure that all custodial staff are in attendance. • Remain current with industry standards and systems related to custodial services. • Deliver messaging and paperwork to key press locations in order to keep custodial staff informed of operational updates, processes, policies, etc. • Support or assist with leading other CSS initiatives as assigned. • Plan, prioritize and manage the work of employees, providing strategic and tactical advice, guidance and coaching. Identify the need for staff resources, participate on staffing committees, and make effective recommendations regarding employee selection. • Manage performance by establishing performance standards, reviewing and evaluating performance and conducting formal performance reviews on an ongoing basis. • Assess staff training and development needs, and ensure that employees receive training required to improve and sustain successful performance. • Investigate, address and resolve employee/labour relations issues, including disciplinary matters. Make decisions or effective recommendations on matters involving possible discipline, discharge and probationary termination. • Foster a productive and harmonious workplace through the promotion of a positive, inclusive teamwork environment, which recognizes the value of all CSS employees. SPECIAL SKILLS: • Proficiency with computers, Internet, and Microsoft Office Applications software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), databases, and custodial services related software applications such as client maintenance management systems (CMMS), OrangeQC, cleaning software, key systems, etc.; ability to adapt to new technologies. • Capacity to embrace change and act as a change champion for others. • Analytical, organizational, planning and problem-solving skills, in order to coordinate and direct the work of custodial staff and to examine alternate possibilities and arrive at the best solution. • Client service aptitude with the ability to consistently deliver excellent client service with an ability to interact professionally and effectively with staff at all levels of the university, faculty, students and members of the public, and to provide clear and accurate information to clients and contacts. • Capable of maintaining strict confidentiality with an ability to recognize and handle confidential information in an appropriate manner. • Receptive to diverse thoughts and alternative perspectives and incorporate them into the work where appropriate. • Ability to work independently and as part of a team, mindful of the interests of other stakeholders. • Ability to maintain composure in a stressful environment. • Ability to remain adaptable in an environment constantly subjected to interruption and change. • Ability to provide consistent, timely and appropriate staff intervention. • Ability to motivate and to create a positive work environment; sensitivity to issues affecting staff. • Ability to write clear, concise and reports. DECISION MAKING: • Collaborate with Manager to decide on content of messaging that is distributed to key press locations. • Assesses the suitability of job candidates and recommends the most appropriate person for hire. • Determines priorities and makes decisions about staff utilization and assignment of work to achieve optimum efficiencies and productivity. • Assesses employees' training needs and makes recommendations for internal or external training to attain proficiency. • Monitors and assess output and the quality or employees' work, and recommends need for formal training or development plans to management and identifies possible performance and/or disciplinary issues. • Problem solving related to custodial procedures. • Allocates and monitors the work of custodial staff. • Determines appropriate actions to handle emergencies in accordance with CSS, Facilities and university procedures, escalating where appropriate. • Assesses and identifies potential inefficiencies with current programs, escalating where appropriate. QUALIFICATIONS: • Post-secondary education in Facilities Management, Business Administration, or a related field combined with relevant experience in supervising/managing unionized custodial staff in an educational or large commercial/industrial setting. • Knowledge of inventory control, custodial procedures, tools and equipment, and practices that operate 24/7. • Competent supervisor as defined under the Occupational Health and Safety Act with practical knowledge of the Occupational Health & Safety Act and how it applies to custodial work. • Satisfactory Criminal Records Check (CRC) and Vulnerable Sector Screening (VSC). • Valid Province of Ontario Class Full G driver's licence and insurable under the university's insurance plan. • Knowledge of the International Sanitary Supply Association (ISSA) and Association of Physical Plant Administrators (APPA) training considered an asset. • Knowledge of programming autonomous equipment considered an asset. • Consideration may be given to an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

title: IT Technician, Creativity Centre - Community Engagement

Halton Hills, located 45 minutes from Toronto, is a unique and vibrant community with over 61,000 people and two well-established library branches. HHPL welcomes more than 250,000 visitors annually and more than 500,000 website visitors. We empower our patrons to learn, read, create, innovate, and experience at our library. We strive to remove barriers and to foster an atmosphere of learning, support, understanding and inclusion. We employ over 35 professionally trained library staff, who go above and beyond to provide stellar service to our patrons and deliver high-quality programs and relevant events. If this excites you, we'd love to continue the conversation. Position Summary The Halton Hills Public Library is seeking an Information Technology Technician who will provide training and support to staff and members of the public to ensure customer service excellence, while bringing a hands-on, experimental approach to learning and a "tinkerer" mindset, with a strong interest in exploring, testing, and troubleshooting using tools and emerging technologies. The Information Technology Technician will provide customer service and support for new technologies for all ages. The position will plan, coordinate, and conduct all ages programming and training sessions on the use of makerspace technologies and consumer devices to support staff and patron knowledge. In addition, they may be called upon to actively resolve end user help requests both in-person, via email or by telephone and work on a public service desk and help patrons of all ages and backgrounds make the greatest use of the library by providing in-depth information, service and advice on print and non-print collections. This position will work out of the Georgetown and Acton Branches and is required to work weekdays, evenings, and weekends. The position will report to the Youth Services Librarian. Position Details These responsibilities indicate the general nature and level of work expected. It is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities required by the incumbent. The incumbent may be asked to perform other duties as required and as the nature of library services evolve. Champion and promote new makerspace technologies and consumer devices to the public and staff Process, plan and provide on-site technology certification and other programs Instruct the public and staff in the use of technology for our Makerspace (Creativity Centre) such as 3D printing, Adobe Creative Cloud, sewing and embroidery machines, and Cricut. Instruct the public and staff in the use of makerspace technologies, consumer devices and social media Develop help sheets and frequently asked questions lists for end users Field incoming help requests from members of the public via email, telephone, and Book a Librarian service in a courteous manner Apply diagnostic utilities to aid in troubleshooting, and machine maintenance in consultation with the I.T. Specialist Plan, conduct and evaluate creative, cultural, dynamic, innovative, and literacy-building programs for all ages, as well as library programming on Makerspace technologies, social media, e-resources, and desktop software Represent the Library at outside events and to community organizations (local events, schools, community centres) Instruct the public and staff in the use of the catalogue and the Library's other online resources such as our website and databases Assist with the development of Makerspace procedures Assist in supervising the work of Community Engagement summer students Serve as a member of the Emerging Technology Committee Perform other job-related duties Hours: Approx. 28 hours per week. Includes weekdays, evenings and weekends in both Acton and Georgetown Branches or at event locations. Compensation: The rate for this position is $36.38 to $43.31 per hour Position Details: This posting is for an existing vacancy in the Community Engagement department Application Deadline: September 27, 2026 at 11:59 pm Start Date: October 2026 Qualifications Essential Minimum education: A Diploma in Computer Science/Information Science or equivalent 6 months - 1 year experience working in a similar position, or equivalent education and experience Superb customer service skills Excellent attention to detail Well-developed library-programming and presentation skills Able to accommodate a variable schedule Able to organize time efficiently Ability to interact pleasantly and courteously with the public and staff, and to promote a harmonious workplace Strong written and oral communication skills. Desirable Additional training in Library techniques or related disciplines Keen interest in emerging technology trends and continuous learning Valid driver's license Access to a vehicle

title: TELUS Pre-Approved CPA Program 2027 - Accounting Opportunity
description: Location: Vancouver, BC, CA, V6B 0M3 Calgary, AB, CA Vancouver, BC, CA Edmonton, AB, CA Toronto, ON, CA Req ID: 56236 Jobs by Category: Students and New Grads Job Function: Co-op & Internship Programs Status: Full Time Schedule: Regular Description Our team and what we'll accomplish together Are you ready to embark on an exciting journey towards a rewarding career in accounting? We are committed to fostering diversity, inclusion, and accessibility, making this opportunity ideal for Indigenous and diverse candidates who are passionate about making a difference in a purpose-led organization. Learn more here: TELUS Pre-Approved CPA Program . At TELUS, we believe in the power of teamwork and collaboration. Partner with experienced TELUS Finance team members, receiving mentorship and guidance throughout the program. Embrace continuous learning, developing a deep understanding of source systems and business processes. *Possible Rotations in the Program include: Corporate Accounting and Financial Reporting Revenue Assurance Internal Audit and SOX Corporate Development Treasury and Investor Relations Taxation Capital Management TELUS Ventures Business Intelligence Financial Planning and Analysis across various teams Qualifications What you bring A post-secondary graduate in Accounting (class of 2026 or 2027) with a passion for pursuing a CPA designation. Highly developed analytical and problem-solving skills. Proficiency in MS Office and G-Suite, with advanced knowledge of Excel. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, enabling you to collaborate effectively with diverse teams. Proven ability to balance work, school, and life commitments, while producing quality work on time. Innovative mindset, eager to learn and adapt in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment. Great-to-haves: Work experience, community involvement, and team engagement. Completion of CPA prerequisite courses. Bilingualism (English/French). title: Registered Practical Nurse
description: Perform nursing procedures consistent with the Standards of Practice and Scope of Practice as defined by the College of Nurses of Ontario. Responsible for administration of medications including narcotics, catheter insertion, maintenance, troubleshooting and discontinuation, wound care; developing appropriate treatments in collaboration with wound care team, ongoing monitoring and evaluation, escalation based on assessments if worsening condition, respiratory assessments leading to initiation of oxygen therapy and medication interventions, documentation in the resident's electronic health record including, progress notes, medication administration and effectiveness, interventions and changes in conditions. Complete all vital signs including neurological. Assist with the assessment of the residents' needs, their plan of care and evaluation of the care provided. Partner with residents and their families in the provision of care. Provide for the residents' emotional and physical comfort and safety. Assess the residents and report significant change(s) in condition to the Registered Nurse. Maintain responsibility for the residents unless the care needs are outside of their scope of practice. Work in collaboration with the Registered Nurse and Physicians to make modifications to resident care plans and treatments as required. Complete appropriate referrals to interdisciplinary team in accordance with the plan of care or changes in resident condition. Perform health training to residents within the realm of his/her knowledge and training. Direct the Personal Support Workers to assist with social or recreational activities for residents. Responsible for personal and vocational growth and development, while remaining up to date on best practice guidelines. Possess strong interpersonal and communication skills with exceptional organizational and leadership ability. • Provide nursing care to residents with acute and chronic illnesses and conditions whose needs are generally stabilized. The RPN will assume the role of team leader per neighborhood, guiding and directing the Personal Support Workers in the provision of high quality and safe resident care. • Two (2) year diploma Registered Nursing Assistant/Registered Practical Nurse and CPR as a part of the core program. Current registration with the College of Nurses of Ontario in good standing. • Minimum of six (6) months' experience required.

title: Diagnostic Medical Sonographer (Ultrasound Technologist)
description: At Canada Diagnostic Centres ("CDC"), we are driven by helping Canadians access diagnostic services and providing remarkable experiences to our patients every day. Our care is compassionate, accurate and timely to help patients make progress in their health journey. We live by our vision of "Remarkable Care. Remarkable Careers." We are looking for recent or upcoming Diagnostic Medical Sonography graduates who are eligible for or registered with the ACMDTT to join our expanding outpatient clinics as full-time, part-time, or casual Ultrasound Technologists. Working collaboratively with radiologists and other healthcare professionals, you'll explain procedures, position patients, adjust equipment, and capture diagnostic images. Bringing compassion and clarity to each patient interaction, you'll help ensure remarkable care every visit. What You'll Be Doing Perform Ultrasound Exams: Conduct routine and specialized sonography imaging under the direction of Radiologists and referring Physicians, while adhering to departmental protocols and guidelines. Provide Remarkable Care: Explain exams and procedures, address questions, ease concerns, and help patients feel comfortable. Collaborate with Clinic Teams: Partner with radiologists and other teams to help deliver a seamless and thoughtful experience. Expand Expertise: Engage in ongoing professional development to refine existing skills, build new competencies, and specialize in additional skillsets such as Interventional, MSK, and Breast. Ensure Compliance: Follow privacy, confidentiality, safety, and other regulatory requirements. Monitor and Troubleshoot Systems: Track ultrasound equipment performance, document findings, and resolve basic issues. Prepare and Maintain Work Areas: Prepare and stock exam rooms for exams and procedures; report low inventory as needed. What We're Looking For Professional Membership: Current registration, or eligibility, with the Alberta College of Medical Diagnostic and Therapeutic Technologists (ACMDTT), or eligibility for registration. Ultrasound Experience: Clinical competency as a generalist sonographer, with an interest in refining and expanding skills in advanced practice areas such as MSK, OB/GYN, vascular and cardiac exams, and interventional procedures. A Compassionate Approach: A history of remarkable care, collaboration, adaptability, and flexibility. What We Offer Competitive Pay: Industry-leading wages and unique additional earning opportunities. Sign-On Bonus: A welcome incentive for joining our team (terms and conditions apply). Relocation Allowance: Financial assistance for eligible candidates to help with moving expenses. Generous Time Off: Vacation, personal days, sick leave, and paid time off for your birthday for full-time and part-time team members. Casual team members receive vacation pay. Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision benefits, plus access to our Employee & Family Assistance Program (terms and conditions apply). Learning & Development: Specialized training opportunities, along with an annual education allowance for part-time and full-time team members. Long-Term Savings Program: RRSP/TFSA plan (terms and conditions apply). Income Protection: Short-term and long-term disability coverage available for part-time and full-time team members. Life Insurance: Coverage to protect you and your loved ones (terms and conditions apply). Professional Licensing Support: Funding available for Sonography Canada and ACMDTT membership fees. Additional Information Students and Recent Graduates: We welcome applications from Diagnostic Medical Sonography students completing their studies in 2026, 2027, or 2028, as well as recent graduates who completed their studies in 2025 and 2026! Position Types: Full-time, part-time or casual options to align with your schedule and career goals. Consistent Schedule: Daytime, Monday to Friday. Work Location: Clinic assignments will be discussed during the candidacy process and guided by operational needs and professional development, with preferences considered where possible. Out-of-Province Applicants: Eligibility for registration with the ACMDTT is required. About Canada Diagnostic Centres With a network of over 50+ community clinics across British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Ontario, we have been a leader and innovator in radiological services for more than 30 years. At the core of our work is a simple belief: Clarity Through Caring. This means diagnostic imaging that is compassionate, accessible, and grounded in quality. In 2025, we supported more than 900,000 patients through their diagnostic journey. Our expertise spans a full range of imaging and interventional services, including MRI, CT, Ultrasound, Echocardiography, Nuclear Medicine, Mammography, X-Ray, Breast Imaging, Bone Mineral Density, Fluoroscopy, Maternal Fetal Medicine, Pediatric Imaging, Gastrointestinal Studies, and image-guided pain management procedures. Our services are delivered by collaborative interdisciplinary teams that bring clarity through caring to life. Inspired by what our teams make possible, we create opportunities for development, provide reliable equipment, and continuously improve how care is delivered. The care we extend to our patients and teams shapes how we welcome applicants. We actively invite applications from all individuals and are committed to equitable hiring practices. If you require accommodations at any stage of the hiring process, please contact us at talentacquisition@canadadiagnostics.ca. Please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted. All applicants must have legal authorization to work in Canada.

title: Human Remains Transport Specialist
description: Human Remains Transport Specialist Ottawa, ON - Eastern Ontario Removal Services (EORS) Full-Time/ Part Time | 12-Hour On-Call Shifts | Paid Training | No Experience Necessary Not every job lets you be the calm, steady presence a family needs on the worst day of their lives. As a Human Remains Transport Specialist with EORS, you will. You'll work in a two-person team responding to calls from hospitals, retirement homes, and private residences across Ottawa - treating every decedent, and every family, with the dignity they deserve. About EORS Since 2003, Eastern Ontario Removal Services has been the National Capital Region's leading removal service for the funeral industry - the largest and longest-running provider in Ottawa. Our unmarked, professionally equipped fleet and trusted relationships with funeral homes, hospitals, and police services are built on one thing: staff who show up with compassion, integrity, and respect every time. Why Join Our Team Paid, hands-on training - no prior experience required Security clearance fully paid for by the company Full-time or part-time schedule Health benefits: dental, vision, and life insurance (for eligible employees working 20hrs a week) Work as part of a supportive two-person team, never alone on a call A genuinely meaningful role - you make a difficult moment easier for grieving families A Day in the Life You'll work 12-hour on-call shifts in pairs. When a call comes in, the dispatcher sends you the details and your team heads to the scene - a hospital, home, or care facility. You'll carry out the removal with care and professionalism, then transport the decedent to different locations for after care. What You'll Do Complete removals of decedents from hospitals, private residences, and retirement/nursing homes Safely operate company vehicles to transport human remains Offer calm, compassionate support to grieving families at the scene Complete funeral home intake paperwork accurately Coordinate with funeral home staff, police, and dispatchers throughout your shift What We're Looking For A kind, presentable, and professional demeanor Strong interpersonal and communication skills Ability to lift up to 100 lbs. and push/pull up to 250 lbs. Comfortable working outdoors in all weather, and available for nights/weekends Good organizational and time-management skills Valid G2 or G driver's licence Clean criminal record French is an asset, not required Compensation & Benefits Competitive hourly wage (training $20 per hr. Wages increase after probation, and again every 6 months up till 2 years of employment) Dental care, vision care, and life insurance Flexible scheduling Paid security clearance and training How to Apply If you're reliable, compassionate, and ready to do work that truly matters, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today with your resume to Lacey@eors.email

title: Dental Hygienist Level 1
description: Calian is proud to continue a long-standing contractual relationship with the Department of National Defence (DND) to provide healthcare services to the Canadian Armed Forces. Through the Health Care Provider Contract, Calian employs health care professionals across Canada who are integral to supporting the health and wellbeing of our military members. Position Overview As a Dental Hygienist at CFB Ottawa, you'll play a critical role in delivering high-quality oral healthcare to the men and women of the Canadian Armed Forces. Working alongside skilled dentists, you'll be a part of a close-knit team focused on supporting the health, well-being, and readiness of Canada's military members. Looking for that work/life balance? This opportunity offers daytime hours only-no evenings, no weekends, and you'll be off for all provincial stat holidays. On top of that, we're offering group benefits program with access to paramedical services and more. You'll also have access paid time off! Responsibilities • Perform scaling, root planning, curettage, polishing procedures, desensitizing agents, occlusal sealants and anti-cariogenic agents • Provide oral hygiene instructions, nutritional counselling and smoking cessation • Conduct periodontal examinations and record clinical findings • Take digital radiographs • Provide administrative support such as updating patient databases, scheduling programs, and maintaining patient records Qualifications • Graduate of an accredited Dental Hygiene program • Registered and in good standing within the province of Ontario (CDHO) • CPR Level C or BLS provider • WHMIS Certification Additional Requirements • Eligible to obtain a Government Security Clearance at the Reliability level Compensation $43 - 46/ hour Vacancy 1 • Graduate of an accredited Dental Hygiene program • Registered and in good standing within the province of Ontario (CDHO)

title: Sonographer Part-Time
description: Almonte General Hospital and Carleton Place & District Memorial Hospital created the Mississippi River Health Alliance (MRHA) in 2016 to formalize their commitment to work together to improve each patient and resident's overall health care experience through a strong, coordinated system of care. An integrated Senior Team leads the two Hospitals, as well as Fairview Manor and Lanark County Paramedic Service which are operating divisions of AGH. Over 600 caring staff, physicians and midwives provide excellent primary, acute and long-term care to citizens of Lanark County, West Ottawa and Renfrew County. The Sonographer produces quality sonographic images on PACS in accordance with Sonography Canada and the College of Medical Radiation and Imaging Technologists of Ontario to ensure accurate diagnosis and treatment for all patients. The incumbent must be a member of Sonography Canada and CMRITO. The Almonte General Hospital/MRHA offers: Competitive Salaries Pension Plan (Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan - HOOPP) Employee and Family Assistance Program …and so much more! Competencies and Personal Attributes Commitment to excellence, quality, and patient/resident safety. Demonstrated caring and empathetic attitude. Ability to meet all demands of the job, both physical and cognitive Ability to work cooperatively and respectfully within a team environment. Must have a satisfactory performance and attendance records Ability to work in a manner that is in compliance with patient/resident and employee safety practices, policies and procedures of the organization. Ability to contribute to a work environment that is conducive to the organizations Workplace Violence and Harassment policy. Mandatory Requirements Current Registration with Sonography Canada and a maintained registry status by obtaining the required 40 hours Continuing Medical Education credits every three years Graduate of an approved Diagnostic Sonography Course Minimum of two (2) years' experience, preferred Must be able to perform Obstetrical Ultrasounds and current experience in Vascular Ultrasounds would be a definite asset. Current CPR
