title: TELUS Pre-Approved CPA Program 2027 - Accounting Opportunity
description: TELUS Pre-Approved CPA Program 2027 - Accounting Opportunity Locations: Vancouver, BC, CA, V6B 0M3 Vancouver, BC, CA Edmonton, AB, CA Calgary, AB, CA Toronto, ON, CA Req ID: 56236 Jobs by Category: Students and New Grads Job Function: Co-op & Internship Programs Status: Full Time Schedule: Regular Description Our team and what we'll accomplish together Are you ready to embark on an exciting journey towards a rewarding career in accounting? TELUS invites you to join our Pre-Approved CPA Program, a three-year rotational program designed to provide practical experiences and develop your core competencies in accounting. We are committed to fostering diversity, inclusion, and accessibility, making this opportunity ideal for Indigenous and diverse candidates who are passionate about making a difference in a purpose-led organization. Learn more here: TELUS Pre-Approved CPA Program . At TELUS, we believe in the power of teamwork and collaboration. As a participant in our Pre-Approved CPA Program, you will have the opportunity to work with a diverse and inclusive team, contributing to the financial and operational excellence of TELUS. Your work will have a meaningful impact on our customers, shareholders and on the communities in which we operate. Finance at TELUS is more than an opportunity to drive financial and operational excellence while creating value for investors, customers and team members. It is also about strengthening the community and taking actions every day to support TELUS' commitment to social capitalism. For example, in 2024, TELUS planted 8 million trees to help mitigate climate change and build a better and more sustainable future. You will join a three-year rotational program designed to meet all of your CPA practical experience requirements while working through your CPA professional education program. You are not doing it alone. You will be part of a national community of TELUS CPA students and alumni, supporting each other in reaching personal and professional goals. As you near the completion of the Program, you will have the opportunity to network with various teams and leaders across TELUS who will help guide you as you transition into a permanent role in the TELUS Finance team. The support you will receive in obtaining your CPA designation includes: Personal mentorship from an experienced TELUS Finance team member. Generous study leave policies. Flexible mobile work arrangements. Financial support for your studies. Well-rounded CPA prep program. What you'll do Though the specific responsibilities will change with the rotation*, you will: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to perform financial analysis, ensuring data integrity and accuracy for effective business decisions. Drive financial reporting, budgeting, analytics, forecasting, and provide financial input to projects and business cases. Partner with experienced TELUS Finance team members, receiving mentorship and guidance throughout the program. Embrace continuous learning, developing a deep understanding of source systems and business processes. *Possible Rotations in the Program include: Corporate Accounting and Financial Reporting Revenue Assurance Internal Audit and SOX Corporate Development Treasury and Investor Relations Taxation Capital Management TELUS Ventures Business Intelligence Financial Planning and Analysis across various teams What you bring A post-secondary graduate in Accounting (class of 2026 or 2027) with a passion for pursuing a CPA designation. Highly developed analytical and problem-solving skills. Proficiency in MS Office and G-Suite, with advanced knowledge of Excel. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, enabling you to collaborate effectively with diverse teams. Proven ability to balance work, school, and life commitments, while producing quality work on time. Innovative mindset, eager to learn and adapt in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment. Great-to-haves: Work experience, community involvement, and team engagement. Completion of CPA prerequisite courses. Bilingualism (English/French). Basic experience using AI tools and technologies to improve productivity and efficiency, with a strong emphasis on responsible and ethical usage. How to Apply: TELUS is committed to accessibility, diversity, and inclusion. If you require accommodation or have any accessibility needs, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your requirements. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals, including Indigenous Peoples, members of visible minorities, persons with disabilities, and candidates of all genders and sexual orientations. We strive to create a workplace that reflects the diversity of our customers and communities, and we actively encourage candidates from underrepresented groups to apply. All applicants must apply directly to TELUS by September 18, 2026 at 11:59 pm EDT. When applying, please ensure you include your cover letter, resume and transcripts . Failure to include all three may result in your application not being reviewed. Applications will be reviewed as they are received. You will receive an automatic email to confirm your application. Salary Range: $57,000-$105,000 Performance Bonus or Sales Incentive Plan: 10% Actual total compensation will be determined based on factors such as knowledge, skills, performance and experience. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, even if the posted salary range doesn't match your expectations. We're open to discussing competitive compensation packages tailored to your experience level and expertise. TELUS offers rewarding benefits, which may vary per job function, such as: Generous company matched pension and share purchase programs Flexibility to work in-office, virtually or a combination of both Opportunity to give back to communities in which we work, live and serve Career growth and learning & development opportunities to develop your skills And much more … A bit about us We're a people-focused, customer-first, purpose-driven team who works together every day to innovate and do good. We improve lives through our technology solutions and foster a culture of innovation that empowers team members to solve complex problems and create remarkable human outcomes in a digital world. You'll find our engaging, high-performance culture personally fulfilling, professionally challenging, and financially rewarding. We're committed to diversity and equitable access to employment opportunities based on ability. Your unique contributions and talents will be valued and respected here. When you join our team, you're helping us make the future friendly. Note for Quebec candidates: if knowledge of English is required for this position, it is because the team member will be asked, on a regular basis, to interact in English with external or internal parties or to use English applications or software as part of their tasks.

title: Maintenance Technician
description: It is a great time to join the Saand team! As a leading glass fabrication Company with 4 facilities (Brockport, Rexdale, London and Ottawa,) we are always looking for first class talent to drive results! WHAT WE DO Founded in 1990, Saand has become the leading glass supplier of commercial and residential Insulated Glass Units, fabricated OEM office furniture components, as well as a major distributor of float glass, laminated glass and mirror in North America. WHY APPLY WITH US? Saand employees enjoy: A company culture and environment that promotes engagement, innovation, inclusion and creativity allowing employees to achieve results! Employee recognition programs with incentives, and the opportunity for growth Not to mention, Saand offers a full and comprehensive benefit package including: Competitive salary Single & family company health & dental benefits Long Term Disability, Life and AD&D insurance RRSP/DPSP Safety boots and prescription safety eye wear entitlement POSITION: Maintenance Technician: Afternoon shift starts 3:30pm LOCATION: Ottawa Facility (2448 Huntley Road, Stittsville, ON) PURPOSE OF POSITION: As the PM Technician you will function in providing both a reactive and proactive, multi-skilled maintenance service on all operational equipment and facilities infrastructure, ensuring that Health, Safety and Environmental requirements are adhered to. Implement and manage continuous improvement and modern manufacturing principals by highlighting deficiencies and recommending changes in training, working practices and processes. RESPONSIBILITIES: Ensures operation of machinery and mechanical equipment by completing preventive maintenance requirements on motors, pneumatic tools, conveyor systems, and production machines; following diagrams, sketches, operations manuals, manufacturer's instructions, and engineering specifications; troubleshooting malfunctions Responds to emergency break downs during the production process. Removes defective parts by dismantling devices; using hoists, cranes, and hand and power tools; determines changes in dimensional requirements of parts by inspecting used parts; using rules, calipers, micrometers, and other measuring instruments. Controls downtime by informing production workers of routine preventive maintenance techniques; monitoring compliance. Fabrication and modification of new and existing equipment Maintain/calibrate measuring tools and equipment. Ensures machinery is locked out in accordance with legislated requirements and the Occupational Health and Safety Act. JOB REQUIREMENTS: Ability to build and repair a variety of mechanical systems Knowledge of computerized machinery Ability to read blueprints and technical specifications Ability to weld effectively Flexibility to work overtime or weekends REQUIREMENTS: 2-3 years of Maintenance Technician experience in a manufacturing plant Saand is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. If you are selected to participate in the recruitment process, please inform Human Resources of any accommodations you may require. Saand will work with you in an effort to ensure that you are able to fully participate in the process

title: Respiratory Therapist
employer: Saskatchewan Health Authority, North East, Recruitment & Retention
description: Description: Respiratory therapists evaluate, treat and manage patients of all ages with respiratory illnesses and other cardiopulmonary disorders in a wide variety of clinical settings. Respiratory therapists must demonstrate behavior and ethics that are consistent with the standards and ethics of all health care professionals. In addition to performing respiratory therapy procedures, Respiratory Therapists are involved in clinical decision making (such as patient evaluation, treatment selection and assessment of treatment efficacy) and patient education. Respiratory Therapists report directly to the Director of Respiratory Services. RRTs, as part of the Saskatchewan Health Authority (SHA), work in hospital, clinical care and community care settings as part of a multidisciplinary health-care team in order to provide the best patient care. Hospital settings include Intensive Care Units (ICU), Neonatal ICU, Pediatric ICU, Emergency Departments, Critical Care Units, and other hospital wards. Community Care Settings include Home Oxygen Suppliers. RRTs work in shifts in order to provide health-care coverage based on the needs of the facility or clinic and this may include days, nights, and weekends. Opportunities to grow as a RRT include taking advanced courses to work in specialized areas and pursuing management and leadership positions. Pay, Incentives and Benefits: Wages: $38.64 - $47.14 /hr May be eligible for Recruitment Incentive up to $50,000 and Relocation up to $3,000 In addition to the above pay bands, the SHA provides a comprehensive benefits package including: Extended Health and Dental benefits Defined-Benefit Pension Plan Life and Disability Insurance Employee and Family Assistance Program Annual Vacation Education Respiratory Therapy diploma (RT) Licenses Advanced Cardiac Life Support Certificate (ACLS) Basic Life Support Health Care Provider Certificate (BLS-HCP) Other Education and Training Neonatal Resuscitation Program (NRP) Other Information Preference to HSAS members as per the SAHO/HSAS Collective Agreement Registered/eligible with the Canadian Society of Respiratory Therapist (CSRT)

description: Position Overview The Drafting Technologist supports the production of accurate, fabrication-ready shop drawings for miscellaneous metals and structural steel projects, including railings, guardrails, stairs, canopies, airshaft frames and gratings, etc. This entry-level role, well suited to a co-op student or recent graduate, uses AutoCAD to translate architectural and structural drawings into detailed fabrication drawings, and Bluebeam to manage markups, redlines, and drawing approvals, under the guidance of senior drafting and engineering staff. The Drafting Technologist works closely with estimating, project management, and fabrication shop personnel, gaining hands-on experience while helping to ensure drawings are accurate, code-compliant, and support efficient production and installation. Reporting Relationship Reports to the Project Manager, with day-to-day guidance and mentorship provided by a Senior Drafting Technologist. Major Functions Shop & Fabrication Drawing Production Assist in preparing shop and fabrication drawings for miscellaneous metals and structural steel components, including railings, guardrails, stairs, and structural connections, using AutoCAD, under the guidance of senior drafting staff. Support the translation of architectural and structural drawings, specifications, and field measurements into accurate, fabrication-ready drawings. Learn to develop connection details, material call-outs, and dimensions in accordance with project specifications and engineering requirements. Assist in producing general arrangement drawings, elevations, sections, and details to support fabrication and installation. Help maintain drawing templates, standard details, and title blocks to ensure consistency across projects. Drawing Coordination & Markup Management Assist in reviewing architectural, structural, and engineering drawings for accuracy, completeness, and constructability. Begin using Bluebeam to manage drawing markups, redlines, and revisions throughout the design and approval process, with support from senior staff. Help track and incorporate comments from engineers, project managers, and clients into revised drawings. Support the preparation and maintenance of shop drawing submittal packages and drawing logs for client and engineer approval. Assist in coordinating design changes and revisions with project management and fabrication teams to maintain schedule. Field Documentation & As-Built Drawings Assist in incorporating field measurements, RFIs, and site conditions into drawing revisions. Support the preparation of as-built and conformed-to-construction drawings following installation. Coordinate with field personnel, under supervision, to confirm dimensions and help resolve discrepancies between drawings and actual site conditions. Quality Control & Drawing Standards Assist with quality checks on drawings to confirm dimensional accuracy, code compliance, and adherence to company drafting standards. Learn and apply applicable codes and standards, including AISC, AWS welding symbols, and the Ontario Building Code, with guidance from senior technologists. Help maintain organized, up-to-date drawing files and revision histories for audit and reference purposes. Cross-Functional Collaboration Work with estimating, project management, and fabrication shop personnel to support accurate pricing and efficient production. Participate in project kick-off and design review meetings to build understanding of project scope and technical requirements. Provide drawing support and clarification to shop and field personnel during fabrication and installation, as directed. Contribute ideas to the continuous improvement of drafting processes, templates, and standards. Key Competencies Currently enrolled in, or a recent graduate of, a Drafting, CAD Design, Architectural/Structural Technology diploma or certificate program (or equivalent); co-op students and new graduates are encouraged to apply. Working knowledge of AutoCAD is required, with a strong willingness to build advanced proficiency on the job. Exposure to Bluebeam Revu (or similar markup software) is an asset; training will be provided. Some prior drafting experience through school projects, co-op terms, or part-time work is an asset. Basic understanding of structural steel and miscellaneous metals fabrication methods, connections, and welding symbols is an asset. Developing ability to read and interpret architectural and structural drawings, specifications, and shop drawings, with a strong aptitude to learn. Familiarity with applicable building codes and industry standards (e.g., AISC, AWS, Ontario Building Code) is an asset. Exposure to Tekla Structures or similar 3D modelling software is considered an asset. Performance Metrics Drawing accuracy: frequency of drawing errors or field-driven revisions after drawings are issued for fabrication. Minimize rework required after drawings are issued for fabrication. Reduce recurring errors identified through quality checks. Drawing turnaround: timeliness of shop drawing production and submittal packages against project schedules. 100% of drawing packages delivered on or before internal deadlines. Standards compliance: adherence to company drafting standards, templates, and applicable codes. 100% compliance with drafting standards on internal quality reviews. Key Competencies: Foundational technical drafting skills (AutoCAD); Bluebeam is an asset. Attention to detail and dimensional accuracy. Blueprint and specification interpretation. Organization and drawing document control. Communication and cross-functional collaboration. Problem solving and adaptability. Time management and ability to meet deadlines. Initiative, self-management, and eagerness to learn. title: Community and Fund Development Lead
description: Position Summary The Community & Fund Development Lead is responsible for coordinating and implementing fund development and community engagement strategies that generate sustainable revenue, foster meaningful community relationships, and increase awareness of the North Okanagan Hospice Society (NOHS). This position supports the organization's mission by delivering high-quality fundraising initiatives, donor stewardship programs, grant activities, community partnerships, events, and communications that align with the Society's strategic priorities. The position builds and maintains strong relationships with donors, sponsors, volunteers, community partners, and supporters while ensuring an exceptional donor and community experience. Working collaboratively across the organization, the position contributes to a culture of teamwork, innovation, and service excellence. As a member of a small non-profit organization, the position provides support to organizational initiatives as required, with all responsibilities contributing to revenue generation, donor stewardship, community engagement, or increased awareness of Hospice services. Key Responsibilities Fund Development & Donor Relations Coordinate the implementation of the Society's annual fund development strategy in alignment with organizational goals and fundraising targets. Build, cultivate, solicit, and steward meaningful relationships with individual donors, sponsors, foundations, service clubs, businesses, and community partners. Identify, develop, and secure new funding opportunities, including major gifts, grants, sponsorships, and community partnerships. Coordinate annual giving initiatives including direct mail campaigns, online fundraising, monthly giving, memorial giving, and other donor engagement campaigns. Develop and implement donor stewardship initiatives that foster long-term relationships, meaningful recognition, and donor retention. Maintain accurate donor records and fundraising data within the donor management system while monitoring fundraising performance and preparing reports as required. Monitor fundraising budgets and campaign performance to maximize revenue generation and return on investment. Strategic Fund Development, Planning & Evaluation Contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of the Society's annual fund development plan in alignment with strategic priorities and revenue goals. Monitor and evaluate fundraising campaigns, donor engagement activities, and community initiatives using key performance indicators and fundraising metrics. Analyze fundraising data, donor trends, and campaign outcomes to identify opportunities for growth, innovation, and continuous improvement. Prepare reports, summaries, and recommendations to support informed decision-making by the Executive Director and Board of Directors. Identify emerging fundraising trends, community needs, and best practices to strengthen the Society's fund development strategies and long-term sustainability. Support the development of annual fundraising goals, campaign calendars, and project timelines to ensure coordinated implementation of fund development activities. Foster a culture of continuous improvement by evaluating the effectiveness of fundraising initiatives and recommending enhancements to maximize community engagement and revenue generation. Grants & Sponsorship Development Research, identify, and pursue government, corporate, foundation, and community grant opportunities that align with organizational priorities. Prepare compelling grant proposals, applications, supporting documentation, and required reporting to funding agencies. Maintain an annual grants calendar to ensure timely submission, reporting, and stewardship of grant-funded initiatives. Develop sponsorship opportunities and customized sponsorship packages that create value for community partners while supporting organizational fundraising objectives. Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with current and prospective sponsors to encourage long-term investment in the Society's mission. Fundraising Events & Community Engagement Coordinate the planning, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of the Society's fundraising events and community engagement initiatives. Lead the coordination of signature fundraising events including Dancing with the Vernon Stars, Hike for Hospice, the Butterfly Release, Kentucky Derby Gala, and other fundraising initiatives as assigned. Support third-party fundraising events and community-led initiatives that benefit the Society. Recruit, orient, coordinate, and recognize volunteers supporting fundraising events in collaboration with the appropriate organizational lead. Represent the Society at community events, networking opportunities, presentations, and stakeholder meetings, promoting the mission and values of Hospice. Foster positive relationships within the community that strengthen awareness, engagement, and support for Hospice services. Marketing, Communications & Public Awareness Coordinate fund development marketing and communication initiatives that increase community awareness, donor engagement, and support for the Society. Develop and maintain engaging content across the Society's social media platforms, ensuring consistent branding, messaging, and storytelling. Collaborate on fundraising campaigns, promotional materials, newsletters, donor communications, and digital marketing initiatives. Support media relations by preparing media releases, public announcements, promotional content, and community communications as required. Monitor communication and social media performance using analytics and engagement metrics to evaluate effectiveness and inform future strategies. Ensure all marketing and communications reflect the values, mission, and visual identity of the North Okanagan Hospice Society. Collaboration & Organizational Support Work collaboratively with the Executive Director, program leaders, administrative staff, volunteers, Board committees, and community partners to advance the Society's mission. Participate actively in staff meetings, strategic planning, training, and organizational initiatives. Support an integrated approach to fundraising, communications, volunteer engagement, programs, and community outreach. Foster a respectful, compassionate, inclusive, and psychologically safe workplace. Maintain confidentiality, professional boundaries, and ethical standards in all interactions. Exercise sound judgment and responsibly manage organizational resources within approved budgets. Provide support during periods of increased organizational activity while maintaining focus on the primary responsibilities of the role. Perform other duties consistent with the purpose, scope, and evolving needs of the position. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications: Education, Training and Experience Required Qualifications: Diploma or bachelor's degree in Fund Development, Business Administration, Communications, Marketing, Public Relations, Non-Profit Management, or a related discipline is preferred. An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience may be considered. Minimum of three (3) years' experience in fund development, donor relations, community engagement, marketing, communications, event management, or a related field, preferably within the non-profit sector. Demonstrated experience coordinating fundraising campaigns, donor stewardship initiatives, sponsorship development, and community events. Experience researching, writing, and managing grant applications and funding reports. Experience developing marketing and communication materials, including digital and social media content. Experience using donor management (CRM) databases to maintain records, generate reports, and support fundraising activities. Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines and competing priorities. Experience working collaboratively with volunteers, community partners, sponsors, and diverse stakeholder groups. Experience working in a hospice, healthcare, or not-for-profit environment is preferred Proficiency in Microsoft 365 and relevant administrative systems Intermediate knowledge of computer hardware and software functions Attention to detail and accuracy required Clear Criminal Record Skills and Attributes: Cultural Competency: Demonstrates respect, sensitivity, and understanding of diverse cultural perspectives and practices. Builds inclusive relationships with donors, volunteers, community partners, and stakeholders while promoting equitable access and participation in Hospice programs and services. Relationship Building : Establishes, cultivates, and sustains positive relationships with donors, sponsors, volunteers, community partners, staff, and Board members. Demonstrates professionalism, integrity, and exceptional donor stewardship while fostering long-term community support for the Society. Communication: Communicates effectively with clarity, professionalism, empathy, and authenticity across diverse audiences. Demonstrates exceptional written communication skills, including grant writing, donor communications, marketing materials, and social media content. Confidently represents the Society through presentations, networking opportunities, and community engagement activities. Collaboration & Teamwork: Works collaboratively with staff, volunteers, Board committees, and community partners to achieve shared organizational goals. Fosters a respectful, inclusive, and supportive team environment while contributing positively to organizational culture. Initiative & Innovation: Demonstrates creativity, resourcefulness, and a proactive approach to identifying new fundraising opportunities, community partnerships, and donor engagement strategies. Applies sound problem-solving, decision-making, and critical thinking skills to improve programs and achieve organizational objectives. Planning & Organization: Demonstrates exceptional organizational and project management skills with the ability to coordinate multiple fundraising campaigns, grants, events, and competing priorities while consistently meeting deadlines and maintaining a high level of attention to detail. Analytical Thinking & Results Orientation : Uses fundraising data, donor insights, and performance metrics to evaluate outcomes, identify trends, and recommend continuous improvements. Demonstrates accountability for achieving fundraising goals while supporting the Society's long-term sustainability. Self-Management: Demonstrates resilience, adaptability, accountability, and sound judgment while managing competing priorities in a dynamic non-profit environment. Maintains confidentiality, professional boundaries, and a commitment to continuous learning and professional growth. Attitude: Models a positive, enthusiastic, and professional attitude that reflects the mission, vision, and values of the North Okanagan Hospice Society. Demonstrates compassion, integrity, and a genuine commitment to building meaningful relationships and strengthening community support for Hospice services. 2 - 3 years of experience

title: Vice-President, Revenue and Strategic Partnerships
description: Title Vice-President, Revenue & Strategic Partnerships Type Permanent, Full-time, 35 hours per week Location Ontario (Toronto, Ottawa) Reports to President & CEO Salary $150,000-185,000 About Us Kinvia, previously known as Canadian Feed the Children, envisions a world in which children, youth, and their communities thrive, realizing their full potential. Kinvia works in partnership with local NGO?s and communities in Uganda, Ethiopia, Ghana, Bolivia, and with Indigenous Peoples in Canada. Kinvia is here with communities who are building local, self-reliant, sustainable systems to provide food for their children, youth, and families across generations. It works in solidarity with communities to impact all areas of nourishment at all stages of their lives, including income generation, education, gender equality, racial justice, and climate impacts. About this opportunity Reporting to the President & Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Revenue & Strategic Partnerships (?VP?) is accountable for advancing its long-term financial sustainability through an integrated, diversified, and partnership-driven revenue strategy aligned with Kinvia?s 10-year strategic directions. As a key member of Kinvia?s Senior Leadership Team, the VP is accountable for the day-to-day operation of the Philanthropy Team and the organization?s annual revenue targets. The VP also advises and supports the President & CEO and the Board to advance Kinvia?s mission and financial sustainability. Mentoring, supporting, and collaborating with a dedicated team, as well as collaborating across teams, the VP ensures donor and constituent relationships are built and stewarded, while providing strategic leadership to the team in executing key initiatives, ensuring vision, growth, and relationship-building are fully realized in practice. Key aspects of this role include revenue generation and diversification, resource mobilization, as well as integrated communications, storytelling, stewardship activities, and brand enablement to ensure that all fundraising communications and engagement strategies effectively support Kinvia?s brand and revenue generation and diversification objectives. Vision A world in which children, youth and their communities thrive, realizing their full potential. Mission Kinvia accompanies children, youth, and their communities as they work to overcome systemic barriers to ensuring their rights to nutritious and culturally appropriate food, fostering wholistic well-being. Kinvia?s Approach Kinvia?s approach is grounded in a community led approach. Kinvia works alongside local partners and communities to support them to achieve self-determined, equitable and sustainable food systems. Our approach also recognizes the importance of working directly or indirectly with the economic, social, environmental and political systems that underpin and influence food systems. Kinvia?s Values Kinvia?s values are how it governs the organization, makes decisions and acts as it undertakes its work together. They also serve as the foundation of its culture, behaviors and core beliefs. Accountability ? Kinvia demonstrates its commitment to trust through responsible actions, a focus on meaningful impact, transparency, and reciprocal accountability. Partnership ? It nurtures collaborative relationships and engages communities in shaping decisions that affect their lives. Inclusiveness ? It diligently works to create safe spaces where diverse perspectives and experiences can inform and direct change. Solidarity ? It uplifts one another and accompany those affected by systems of oppression and marginalization. Respect ? Kinvia values the dignity of people and uphold human rights. Humility ? Kinvia is on a continuous journey of healing, growth and discovery, and are committed to creating spaces where they can listen to and learn from each other. Impact Report To read Kinvia?s 2024-2025 Impact Report, please visit: https://kinvia.ca/who/impact-financials/ Where Kinvia Works Kinvia works with local community-based partners in Bolivia, Ethiopia, Ghana, Uganda and with 24 Indigenous partners in Canada. Our work is centred in supporting self-determined, equitable and sustainable food systems by working with communities, particularly women and youth on: Food production, harvesting and processing through sustainable agricultural practices and the use of indigenous seeds Livelihood and job creation Financial inclusion Social inclusion and equity in food systems, including gender transformative change in food systems Tradition and culture in food systems Nutrition Education Community governance structures and leadership Tackling the root causes of poverty and homelessness among Bolivian children and youth. To learn more, please visit: https://kinvia.ca/where/ Responsibilities Revenue Diversification & Growth, Strategic Partnerships & External Influence Provide executive leadership for Kinvia?s integrated revenue diversification, growth, and strategic partnerships strategy, aligned to the organization?s 10-year strategic vision and annual operating priorities. Lead the evolution from reliance on traditional fundraising channels toward a balanced, resilient revenue mix that includes major gifts, philanthropy, partnerships, institutional funding, and innovative revenue models. Ensure clear revenue growth pathways, multi-year forecasting, and financial sustainability in collaboration with the senior leadership team. Serve as organizational lead for monitoring external trends in philanthropy, development, and social impact financing to ensure Kinvia remains adaptive, competitive, and future-ready. Champion an integrated resource mobilization model that aligns fundraising, strategic partnerships, communications, brand, and impact storytelling in service of revenue growth, influence, and long-term engagement. Embed an equity-informed and community-centered approach to resource mobilization, evolving traditional fundraising models to prioritize dignity, reciprocity, and community agency, while addressing systemic power imbalances in how resources are generated and shared. Philanthropy, Donor Stewardship, Strategic Partnerships & Resource Mobilization Serve as the senior organizational steward of Kinvia?s long-standing donor and partner relationships, ensuring trust, reciprocity, and shared purpose remain central to all revenue-generating activities. Provide strategic oversight and co-leadership to the Director, Philanthropy & Resource Mobilization in advancing major gifts, foundations, corporate partnerships, institutional funding, and other priority revenue streams. Work in close collaboration with the President and CEO and personally cultivate and maintain select high-value relationships with donors, partners, and funders, acting as a senior representative and relationship-builder for Kinvia. Ensure strong donor and partner stewardship, prospect development, and relationship management systems that prioritize retention, growth, and long-term commitment. Work in close partnership with the VP, Programs & Partnerships to co-design funding and partnership strategies that are aligned with program priorities, country strategies, in-country funding opportunities, impact objectives, and community accountability. Support and activate Board members, committees, and volunteer leaders to extend Kinvia?s relationship capital, networks, and revenue-generating capacity in ways that are strategic, values-aligned, and appropriate to governance roles Integrated Fundraising, Communications & Brand Enablement Provide executive oversight to the Director, Integrated Fundraising & Communications, ensuring that fundraising communications, brand, and engagement strategies effectively support revenue diversification objectives. Ensure Kinvia?s brand and communications strengthen revenue, influence, and trust, while deepening brand equity, amplifying impact, and reflecting the values, voices, and leadership of the communities we work alongside. Offer strategic counsel to the President & CEO and Board on reputation, positioning, and communications risks, including issues and crisis communications as required. Ensure consistent, values-aligned messaging across donor, partner, sector, and public audiences that reflect Kinvia?s identity, commitments, and impact. Oversee high-level performance and integration across annual giving, digital engagement, storytelling, and stewardship channels without direct operational management. Leadership Governance & Organizational Impact Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to the President & CEO and an active contributor to Senior Leadership Team decision-making. Support the Board of Directors through clear reporting, insight, and strategic framing related to revenue, risk, and opportunity. Foster strong cross-functional collaboration across Programs & Partnerships, Finance & Operations, and Resource Mobilization to ensure alignment between strategy, resources, and impact. Help position Kinvia as a sector leader in sustainable, ethical, and impact-driven resource mobilization. People and Culture & Values Provide strong, empowering leadership to a high-performing advancement and partnerships team through the leadership of two Directors, fostering shared accountability across revenue, partnerships, and programs. Model and reinforce a culture of trust, accountability, learning, and innovation. Support talent development, succession planning, and organizational resilience within the advancement function. Uphold and advance Kinvia?s commitments to equity, anti-racism, anti-oppression decolonization, and community accountability in all revenue-related practices. Operations, Oversight and Accountability Oversees development and communications departments? budgets and maintains executive accountability for advancement-related revenue targets, budgets, forecasting, and performance reporting. Ensure strong systems, controls, and ethical standards for donor stewardship, data management, and compliance. Oversee effective use of fundraising and CRM systems (e.g., Blackbaud NXT) in collaboration with Directors. Prepare high-level reports and recommendations for the President & CEO and Board of Directors. The Candidate: The ideal candidate?s career demonstrates progressive advancement into senior fundraising and leadership roles, including overseeing staff and ideally reporting to a board on fundraising matters. Candidates should have a breadth of experience across the areas in the portfolio, including storytelling, digital engagement and leveraging an organization?s brand to support donor engagement and revenue generation, and with relationship-based fundraising across multiple revenue streams including annual giving, mass market, major gifts and with individuals, foundations, and corporations. As a strategic, systems-thinking leader, candidates have strong financial and budgetary acumen, including managing budgets and with multi-year planning and forecasting, relevant charity regulations, and of CRA guidelines. As a senior executive, you also have experience leading through complexity, change and constraint while maintaining focus on long-term sustainability. Your engaging, honest, and transparent communications style is evident by how you cultivate and maintain strong and trusting relationships with donors and partners, and with your colleagues, direct reports, and Board members. Candidates must demonstrate strong alignment with Kinvia?s mission and values, including a commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, decolonization, anti-racism, and anti-oppression, demonstrated cultural knowledge, humility, and sensitivity, and the ability to engage respectfully and collaboratively with diverse communities, including Indigenous partners in Canada and global partners across Kinvia?s programs. While the Search Committee recognizes that it is unlikely that any one individual will possess all the desired qualifications in equal measure, in addition to the above, the ideal candidate should have the following: Progressive senior leadership experience in fundraising, advancement, or revenue development, with demonstrated success growing and diversifying revenue. Proven ability to lead through complexity, change, and constraint while maintaining focus on long-term sustainability. Deep expertise in major gifts and relationship-based fundraising; experience across multiple revenue streams required. Strong strategic, financial, and systems-thinking capabilities, including experience with forecasting and multi-year planning. Exceptional relationship-building skills with donors, partners, executives, and Boards. Demonstrated ability to lead and empower senior leaders and build high-performing, collaborative teams. Excellent communication, influence, and executive presence. Demonstrated commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, decolonization, anti-racism, and anti-oppression. Experience working closely with a non-profit Board of Directors. CFRE designation is considered an asset. French or Spanish language skills considered an asset. Willingness to travel occasionally and work flexible hours as required. A strong alignment with Kinvia?s values and a desire to make a meaningful difference. Location/Work Hours: While Kinvia is remote first work environment it requires the successful candidate to be based in Toronto or Ottawa and be available to work occasional evenings or weekends to accommodate fundraising events, donor meetings across time zones, and urgent deadlines. The role also requires candidates to be able and willing to travel domestically and internationally. Candidates must be legally eligible to work in Canada. What we offer: Join our team and enjoy a range of benefits designed to support your professional growth and personal well-being: Flexible Work Environment: Embrace a work-life balance with our remote work options. Health & Dental Benefits : Comprehensive coverage to ensure your health and wellness. Mental Health Day : Two employer-supported mental health days per year to help you rest, recharge, and care for your wellbeing. Pension Program: Secure your future with our employer-matched pension plan. Summer Hours & Holiday Program: Enjoy flexible summer schedules and extended holiday periods. Generous Time Off: Benefit from personal days, vacation, and sick leave to recharge and refresh. Volunteer Opportunities: Make a difference with paid volunteer days. Parental Leave Top-Up: Additional support during your parental leave. Learning and Development Support: Invest in your career with our continuous learning and professional development opportunities. Inclusive Culture: Be part of a workplace that is committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, decolonization, anti-racism, and anti-oppression. How to Apply: To learn more about this impactful leadership opportunity with Kinvia, please submit your application: https://kinvia.bamboohr.com/careers/72 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, please apply as soon as possible. We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those under consideration will be contacted. The position will remain open until the successful candidate has been selected. __________________________________________________________________ ??Kinvia is committed to inclusive, accessible and barrier-free employment practices and to creating a workplace that reflects and supports the diversity of our community. We encourage and welcome applications from qualified applicants including members of racialized groups, Indigenous Peoples, women, persons with disabilities, and persons of any sexual orientation or gender identity. Please let us know if you require an accommodation and we will work with you to ensure a barrier-free hiring process. For further information about Accessibility or Accommodation process at Kinvia, please contact our People and Culture Department. ? 5 - 10 years of experience

title: Independent Living Assistant - Relief
description: Under the supervision of the Site Manager and under the direction of clients, the Independent Living Assistant (ILA) assist adults who have physical disabilities with activities of daily living by performing personal support services. This includes tasks involved with personal care and hygiene, general housekeeping, and meal preparation to support independent living, dignity and choice of lifestyle. Summary of Duties Under the direction of the client, provide personal care assistance including: Transfers and lifts Morning and nighttime routines Dressing[MH1.1]/undressing, including medical aids (i.e. braces etc.) Light housekeeping duties Meal preparation including serving, feeding as required and clean-up Peri-care, bowel and bladder care, catheterization, condom application and emergency procedures Attend shifts and bookings punctually and unscheduled booking requests as promptly as possible. Record booking time used, booking changes and cancellations accurately and promptly. Record work hours in the sign-in sheets accurately. Read communication books, memos, bulletin boards and other communications each day at work. Complete communication report, injury report and all other generally used forms accurately, clearly and within the required timeframe. Share and accept assigned bookings and unscheduled requests, assisting colleagues during downtime. Ensure the safety of clients and self during service provision. Communicate relevant and necessary information about clients and service provision issues to the appropriate individual(s). Maintain full knowledge of and ask clarifying questions related to all organizational policies and procedures, equipment, transfer and lifting techniques and individual clients? routines. Maintain appropriate boundaries and preserve the confidentiality and privacy of clients. Communicate relevant service-related information clearly and promptly to clients. Collaborate with colleagues to identify and solve minor service provision issues, respond to client requests and provide flexible service. Assist and participate in the orientation and assigned training of new employees. Carry out assigned cleaning of shared employee facilities. Attend, participate in and read the minutes of site and organization-wide staff meetings. Attend and participate in, or notify the manager of a scheduling conflict for, all assigned training and development. Mental and Emotional Demands of the Role Ability to remain calm, patient and professional when responding to challenging or unexpected situations. Ability to provide compassionate support while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries. Ability to adapt to changing client needs, routines and schedules. Ability to manage the emotional demands of supporting individuals with physical disabilities and varying levels of independence. Ability to exercise sound judgment and seek assistance when required. Qualifications/Skills Three to five years? experience providing attendant care services in a community based or home care environment. Ability to listen and follow the directions of clients. Able to adapt to changes in clients? routines and booking schedules due to emergencies or unanticipated activities. Excellent communication skills and able to communicate respectfully and professionally with clients and colleagues Knowledge and understanding of the Independent Living Philosophy Ability to take initiative Personal Support Worker certification form recognized school considered an asset This job description indicates the general nature and level of work expected. It is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities required by the incumbent. Incumbents may be asked to perform other duties as required. 1 - 2 years of experience

Health Benefits Plan, including Extended Health, Dental & Vision coverage, Basic Life Insurance, Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Benefits and Employee Assistance Programs. Coordinate meetings for the executive leadership team by preparing agendas and materials, attending meetings, recording minutes, and tracking action items to completion. Prepare and coordinate executive reports, presentations, memorandums and other materials, ensuring accuracy, quality, and timely delivery. Respond to requests and inquiries in a professional, and customer-focused manner. title: Marketing Lead
address: 185 Davenport Road, Toronto, ON, M5R 1J1
description: Salary Range $100,000 - $150,000 This posting is for an existing vacancy. We do not use artificial intelligence to screen, assess, or select applicants. The Short Version You'd be our marketing function. Not a marketing team member - the function. One person, senior, with the mandate and the budget to decide what we say, how it looks, and where it runs. That's either the most appealing thing you've read this month or a red flag. We'd rather you know now. Why This Isn't an Agency Job At an agency you'd touch twelve brands and own none of them. Here you own one, end to end: the strategy, the words, the visuals, the campaign, and the number it moved. You'll see a piece of work from a half-idea in a Tuesday meeting through to the metric it changed a quarter later. Very few marketers get that loop, and it's the fastest way we know to get good. You'll report to our Founder, sit close to our Executive Management team, and have real authority over the brand. When you say we're not doing something, we're not doing it. What You'd Actually Do Own the marketing strategy and the budget behind it Write - properly. Editorial, campaign, product, the occasional thing under someone else's name Design and ship the assets. You'll art-direct yourself most of the time Run our content engine end to end: what we publish, why, and whether it works Use AI tooling the way a craftsperson uses a jig - to move faster on the parts that don't need you, so you can spend your judgment where it counts Bring in freelancers and contractors when the work outgrows one pair of hands, and manage them well Tell us honestly what's working and what isn't Who We Think This Is We're looking for an unusual combination, and we know it. You've probably got two of these deeply and can hold your own in the others: Journalism or editorial. You can find the story, ask the uncomfortable question, and structure an argument. You've worked to a deadline that didn't move. Design and graphics. You can build the asset, not just brief it. Figma or Adobe, and taste that shows in the work. AI fluency. You've integrated generative tools into a real workflow and formed opinions about where they help and where they quietly make things worse. Marketing outcomes. You've owned a number, not just a deliverable. Senior-level judgment matters more to us than years. If you've spent three years running a small brand well, that may beat eight years in a large one. Experience Requirement 1 Experience Requirement Experience Requirement Experienced in the following professions: Online Marketing Manager Brand Manager Marketing and Communication Manager

title: Delivery Program Assistant
description: Delivery Program Assistant Parkdale Community Food Bank Department: Delivery Program Location: In-Person (5 Brock Avenue, Toronto) Employment Type: Part-Time 16 - 20 hours per week. Thursday - Saturday. Rate: $27.20 per hour This is an existing vacancy. We are currently seeking the ideal candidate to join our Delivery Team as the Delivery Program Assistant. This position supports our delivery program in a variety of ways, including inventory management assistance, supervising volunteers, working with the drop-in team to maximize efficiencies and supporting pick ups and deliveries on a daily basis. If this sounds like the right position for you, please see details and application instructions below. Who We Are Parkdale Community Food Bank (PCFB) is a non-profit, registered charity in the heart of Toronto?s Parkdale neighbourhood. Every month, our programs support more than 17,000 individuals with access to nutritious food and community support. We believe joy is fundamental to nourishment, and our mission is to create a hunger-free community where everyone has a place at our table, with barrier-free access to food they actually want to eat. About the Delivery Program PCFB founded one of the first completely free grocery delivery programs in Toronto back in 2020, to reach community members who couldn?t leave their homes during the pandemic. The program has kept going since, now serving people who face mobility or health barriers to visiting the food bank in person. Clients place weekly orders based on what?s available, and this role is what makes sure those orders actually reach their door. Mission of This Role For a lot of our Delivery Program clients, the Delivery Program Assistant is the only person from PCFB they?ll see face to face. The Delivery Program Assistant brings more than groceries. They carry our mission of dignity and joy in nourishment straight to someone?s door, often noticing the small things, a favourite snack, a treat someone mentioned once, that turns a simple delivery into a moment of real care. When a client isn?t able to come to the food bank, you make sure the food bank still comes to them. This role reports to the Delivery Program Manager for daily operations. They split their time between the road (pickups and deliveries) and the warehouse (prepping, sorting, and organizing donations for the team), with the exact mix shifting depending on the season and what the program needs that week. Responsibilities Operations Pick up donations around the Toronto area, coordinated by the Delivery Program Manager. Deliver groceries to community members enrolled in the Delivery Program, including covering driver routes over the summer when the team needs extra hands. Adjust pace and planning around seasonal volume shifts. Winter is the busiest stretch for deliveries (50%+ above baseline), and pickups spike heavily over the holidays. Resource and Donation Management Prepare incoming resource donations for the packing team, sorting through boxes and flagging what goes to Delivery versus Drop-In. Set aside high-value or requested items like coffee, condiments, and treats, for the clients who?d appreciate them most, drawing on knowledge built through packing and client audits. Receive and organize food donations, including sorting Daily Bread Food Bank deliveries and setting aside specialty items for volunteers to pack. Keep the warehouse shelves organized and restocked throughout each shift so packing volunteers can find what they need quickly. Track incoming donations in the team?s Discord channel. Volunteer and Community Support Support volunteers who need a hand across the warehouse, kitchen, drop-in, or delivery team. Answer phones and greet visitors, directing them to the right person or resource. Build relationships with clients through the client audit process, one of the more regular points of direct client contact in this role. Qualifications Must-Haves A valid G driver?s licence and comfort navigating Toronto for pickups and deliveries. Experience in a customer-facing role; regularly interacting with clients and volunteers The ability to juggle multiple moving pieces at once and stay highly organized. Comfort being the visible face of PCFB in the community, including appearing in photos donors sometimes take during pickups Nice-to-Haves Familiarity with Toronto?s food donation and supplier landscape Experience or training related to workplace health and safety Comfort using Discord or similar team communication tools AI is not used at any stage of our hiring process. The Parkdale Community Food Bank is committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible environment where employees feel valued and respected, and where every employee has the opportunity to realize their potential. As such, we welcome and encourage applicants who identify as racialized persons, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, and persons across the spectrum of sexual orientation and gender identities and have lived-experience. If you are a person with a disability and require accommodation and/or assistance during the application process, please contact us in advance. We strive to provide reasonable accommodations whenever requested. Information received relating to accommodation requests will be treated with confidentiality. To apply, please email your resume and cover letter in one pdf document to info@pcfb.ca with the subject line ?(Your Name) - Delivery Program Assistant?. Please note the application deadline of August 3rd 2026. Early applications are encouraged.

This dynamic senior-level role encompasses strategic donor engagement, creative relationship-building, and inspiring team leadership, with a strong emphasis on securing game-changing gifts and partnerships, as well as managing development staff and thriving in a vibrant, fast-paced organizational environment. The successful candidate will cultivate and manage an exciting portfolio of major-gift donors and prospects, including visionary individuals and impactful foundations, who share our commitment to supporting young adults in living their lives as they choose. The ideal candidate is a relationship-building superstar with 5+ years of progressive MG fundraising experience, a proven track record of closing 5 and 6-figure gifts, natural team leadership abilities, a talent for navigating complex environments with diverse stakeholders, experience building strong foundation partnerships, an entrepreneurial approach, skills in uncovering compelling prospect opportunities, and exceptional expertise in donor relations and stewardship that turns supporters into lifelong advocates. RESPONSIBILITIES: Major Gift Fundraising and Leadership -- 80% ? Develop and execute major gift strategies across identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship, with annual targets of $1.5M?$2M. ? Manage a portfolio of 100?150 major gift prospects and maintain accurate moves management. ? Lead complex major gift solicitations, including securities, life insurance, grants, multi-year agreements, and transformational gifts. ? Prepare strategic, tailored proposals, presentations, briefing materials, correspondence, and gift agreements. Volunteer Management and Partnership: ? Partner with and coach senior fundraising volunteers, providing orientation, prospect briefings, and strategic guidance on cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. ? Develop and implement customized donor journeys to support donor management and stewardship strategies and activities Foundation and Corporate Relations: ? Research, qualify and manage relationships with individuals, major foundations and corporate partners for gifts of $50,000+ ? Write and prepare major proposals and multi-year partnership agreements ? Meet regularly with foundation program officers, corporate executives, and major individual donors to support the programs and strategic initiatives of Stella's Place Community Engagement and Strategic Networking: ? Actively lead and attend high-level community events and major donor engagement opportunities ? Cultivate impactful event plans and follow-up engagement opportunities ? Research event attendees in advance and develop sophisticated strategies and executions to build cultivation pipelines. ? Brief senior leadership and volunteers with comprehensive briefing notes and follow-up plans ? Collaborate with the Chief Development Officer to create strategy and lead the execution of major gift cultivation and stewardship plans ? Partner with and mentor other fundraising staff to execute comprehensive revenue generation strategies focused on Stella's Place priorities Planning, Administration and Team Leadership: (20%) Strategic Planning: ? Collaborate with the Chief Development Officer to set annual and long-term major gift revenue plans and goals ? Stay informed on Stella's Place projects and strategic initiatives to effectively discuss them with donors and prospects Database Management and Reporting: ? Maintain accurate records. Write and submit customized impact reports for major donors Team Collaboration: ? Manage direct report(s) in strategy, goal setting and execution ? Participate actively as a member of an integrated development team; engage positively with other stakeholder groups and cultivate strong professional relationships with members of other departments ? Assist in other duties as assigned in advancing the goals of the development team and Stella's Place QUALIFICATIONS/REQUIRED EXPERIENCE: ? Minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in fundraising with a demonstrated track record of closing 5 and 6-figure gifts required ? The ability to structure complex financial gifts for sophisticated funders ? Experience in team-building and managing direct-report relationships Essential Skills: ? Excellent organization, planning and time management skills combined with a strong attention to detail ? Superb critical and analytical thinking, decision-making and problem-solving skills with an ability to tell a story through metrics ? Excellent oral and written skills with a demonstrated ability to write effectively and persuasively, and present to diverse groups. Experience with public speaking/presentations is an asset ? Strong computer skills, including experience with Google Docs and online applications ? The ability to conduct high-level discovery calls and sophisticated donor meetings ? Strategic thinker and exceptional listener, genuinely interested in others Preference will be given to candidates with: Education and Certifications: ? A university degree or college diploma in fundraising, or a related field, OR 5+ years' experience in a major gift role ? Gift Planning courses and/or a CFRE designation are an asset Additional Preferred Qualifications: ? Experience developing and implementing major gift and campaign strategies ? Strong understanding of Raiser's Edge NXT or equivalent donor/CRM database; proficiency with Raiser's Edge is preferred ? Interest in or lived experience in supporting young adults and/or mental health ? Existing experience managing and mentoring development staff WORKPLACE, HOURS & REPORTING: Stella's Place is an innovative, award-winning, designed facility located in the vibrant neighbourhood of Queen West and Bathurst. This is a full-time, hybrid, senior leadership position working 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday, including 3 in-office days per week. As a key leader of the development team, occasional weekend and evening work will be required in response to events, donor needs, and strategic initiatives. SALARY & BENEFITS: $99,000-$110,000/ year - commensurate with experience Stella's Place offers a competitive annual salary, and professional development, to support your career growth. We offer a comprehensive rewards package including medical, dental and vision health benefits, which start immediately. Stella's Place offers 3 weeks of vacation and 15 personal days in year one, increasing to 4 weeks of vacation in year two. APPLICATION: Please submit your CV and Cover Letter by Tuesday, September 15, 2026. We thank all applicants who apply. Only those progressing to the next stage will be contacted. Minimal AI is used during the recruitment. DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND ACCOMMODATION: Stella's Place is committed to having a workforce that reflects the diversity of the City of Toronto in general and of our participants in particular. Stella's Place is committed to inclusive, barrier-free hiring practices. Stella's Place commits to supporting persons with disabilities in applying and will provide reasonable and appropriate accommodation at all stages of the hiring process, in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code, to ensure the equal and fair assessment of all job applicants. Applicants are asked to make any accommodation requests in advance. 5 - 10 years of experience

title: Senior Manager, Annual Campaigns & Development Operations
description: Position Title: Senior Manager, Annual Campaigns & Development Operations Location: Toronto - Hybrid 3 days / week in office Salary: $95,000-$102,000/ year OVERVIEW: Reporting directly to the Chief Development Officer (CDO), the hands-on Senior Manager, Annual Campaigns & Development Operations, will increase annual funds, develop and execute the Annual Campaign, manage appeals, oversee and create efficiencies in development system tools, and operationally prepare the development department for future growth. Our visionary organization is ready for the next stage of its evolution as one of Canada?s leading mental health facilities for young adults, raising $4-5M+ annually to sustain our vision, mission and innovative program model. This multi-faceted role is ideal for a leader interested in bringing their expertise to a smaller organization with a big future. You will bring fresh ideas, enthusiasm and innovation to an agency ready to take its Annual and other fundraising programs to the next level. POSITION: The successful candidate will develop and lead all Annual Campaign fundraising activities for gifts, driving the acquisition and managing the stewardship of monthly donors. Reporting to the Chief Development Officer (CDO), This Senior management role will help supervise and grow the Annual Campaign Team, overseeing development officer(s), student placements, and the Mid-Level Giving Officer. You will serve as the team lead interfacing with and overseeing the Design & Digital Media team, which will support the department's marketing outreach efforts. You will mentor and/or collaborate with all members of the development team. You will collaborate with the other departments and oversee contracted support as needed. Operationally, this role ensures that quality standards are adhered to for all fundraising activities, including oversight and direction of general administration, stewardship tracking, moves management, budgeting for the Annual Campaign, gift processing, oversight of the CRM database, its manual and its reports, and oversight of licensed tools for development support. RESPONSIBILITIES: Annual Campaign Fundraising & Donor Engagement (55%) ? Develop and execute Annual fundraising strategies and achieve Annual revenue targets across direct mail, digital, monthly, mid-level, legacy, and tribute giving. ? Manage and steward a portfolio of 400+ annual donors, with a focus on retention and increased giving, and with the support of direct reports. ? Lead direct mail and digital campaigns, including donor acquisition, retention, renewal, and moves management. ? Oversee donor thanking and mass-personalization strategies, including the use of automation tools. ? Monitor campaign performance, analyze trends, and recommend strategies to improve results; provide regular reporting to the CDO. Digital Communications as it supports Annual Campaign Execution (15%) ? .Develop and manage an integrated communications calendar aligned with fundraising, stewardship, events, and donor engagement. ? Manage departmental donor lists and oversee fundraising content and presence across the website, social media, and third-party fundraising platforms. ? Oversee the ongoing maintenance of the department?s website and presence on social media accounts and Comms content as fulfilled by the Design & Digital Communications Team ? Working with Development Officers, manage and update our presence on third-party fundraising platforms, i.e. Canada Helps, Race Roster, PayPal Giving Fund, Benevity, etc. Reporting and Database Administration (25%) ? Lead database administration and provide database training and support. to other team members as required. ? Track and import gift agreements and support finance with audit requests. ? Develop fundraising reports, KPIs, donor recognition lists, and performance reporting for the CDO. ? Prepare donor recognition listings for annual reports, the website, digital donor lists, and the digital wall. ? Maintain updates and troubleshoot the onsite digital donor wall. ? Lead gift processing (mainly automated for under 2K gifts per year) according to Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Guidelines, prepping manual tax receipts as needed and reconciling event revenue. ? Liaise with the Finance Manager on monthly bank reconciliations and departmental budgets as needed. ? Manage operational contracts, licenses and relationships with suppliers/consultants, including expenditure oversight. ? Oversee fundraising systems, vendors, and volunteers. Other Duties as Needed (5%) ? Assist in other duties as assigned in advancing the goals of the development team and Stella?s Place. QUALIFICATIONS: ? Minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in fundraising with a demonstrated track record in Annual Campaigns Moves Management ? At least 2+ years of experience in managing direct-report relationships ? Raiser's Edge database proficiency with Raiser's Edge gift processing is required; RE certification is preferred; NXT experience is an asset ? Strong digital & direct mail skills: Experience with Mailchimp, Importacular, Red Arc Letterbox, database importing and exporting is an asset ? Strong computer literacy: Google Office ( Gmail, Google Docs and Google Sheets), Excel and PowerPoint skills are an asset ? Demonstrated organizational and analytical ability ? Excellent relationship-building skills, with demonstrated ability to collaborate with colleagues and volunteers, and connect with donors ESSENTIAL SKILLS: ? Excellent detail focus, and a love of data and the insights data can drive ? Organization, planning and time management skills ? Extremely effective interpersonal skills with a professional presence and manner, and capable of exercising independent judgment, initiative, and flexibility ? Demonstrated ability to think strategically, work proactively, and manage competing priorities in a complex and evolving environment WORKPLACE, HOURS & REPORTING: Stella's Place is an innovative, award-winning, designed facility located in the vibrant neighbourhood of Queen West and Bathurst. This is a full-time, hybrid, senior leadership position working 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday, including 3 in-office days per week. As a key leader of the development team, occasional weekend and evening work will be required in response to events, donor needs, and strategic initiatives. You will receive regular coaching, development, and performance feedback from the Chief Development Officer and provide the same to your direct reports. SALARY & BENEFITS: $95,000-$102,000/ year - commensurate with experience Stella's Place offers a competitive annual salary, commensurate with experience and professional development, to support your career growth. We offer a comprehensive rewards package including medical, dental and vision health benefits, which start immediately. Stella's Place offers 3 weeks of vacation and 15 health days in year one, increasing to 4 weeks of vacation in year two. Please submit your CV and Cover Letter by Tuesday, September 15, 2026.
